Title: Launch of the 'Sustainability Dimension' of Agenda BC
Subtitle: Opening speech for the launch of the Sustainability Dimension of the Agenda BC#
text: Opening speech for the launch of the Sustainability Dimension of the Agenda BC# Fernanda Nechio, Deputy Governor for International Affairs and Corporate Risks Management September 8, 2020 Good morning, good afternoon and good evening to all of you with us today. Welcome to the launch of the Sustainability Dimension of the Central Bank of Brazils Agenda BC#. In my brief initial remarks, I will focus on three main points: the Central Bank of Brazil's responsibility in face of structural changes in the economy; the emergence of socio-environmental risks and their implications for the monetary authority; and the new Sustainability Dimension of the Agenda BC#. The Central Bank of Brazils responsibility Turning to the first point, the Central Bank of Brazils (BCB) objectives are to ensure price stability and the strength and efficiency of the National Financial System. In order to achieve these objectives, the Central Bank needs to remain at the frontier on its actions, responding to shocks and risks, present and future; to the evolution of society's demands; and to structural changes in the economy. For brevity, the BCB's action plan must be dynamic and comprehensive. The current dimensions and actions of the Agenda BC# respond to these needs. PIX and Open Banking are examples of prompt responses to technological changes in payment systems and to the evolution of society's demands in search of a swift, competitive and safe financial system. The emergence of socio-environmental risks and their implications for the monetary authority But how does this relate to the climate agenda? Similar to our recent actions in the technological front, the new Sustainability Dimension of the Agenda BC# was developed to respond to yet another set of structural changes in the economy. The new dimension responds to the emergence of new risks and demands from the society. It is clear that climate events that were previously considered rare have become more frequent. Such events are accompanied by changes in main economic variables in the relevant horizon for monetary policy, in addition to bringing significant risks to the financial system. Increasingly frequent climate shocks  wildfires, droughts, floods, extreme temperatures  affect relative prices in the economy, and therefore, may have an impact on our monetary policy decisions. These same extreme events put the National Financial System at risk, and may change the demand for currency, physical assets and loan collaterals values, in addition to bringing high financial costs to our society. Thus, in order to fulfil the Central Bank of Brazils mandate determined by law of ensuring price stability and guaranteeing the soundness and efficiency of the National Financial System, we must prepare and respond appropriately to these structural changes in the economy. The Central Banks policy making must consider socioenvironmental risks and the impact of extreme events on our economy and financial system. The Sustainability Dimension of the Agenda BC# With that in mind, today we launch a new dimension to our strategic agenda. 2 The new Sustainability dimension of the Agenda BC# is dynamic and comprehensive, embracing all areas of the Central Bank. The actions included in the sustainability pillar include social and environmental responsibility measures geared towards both the financial system and the Central Bank. The role of central banks and the financial market in promoting sustainable finance and mitigating the effects of climate risks is a rapidly evolving theme in Brazil and worldwide. We must be on this frontier. Thus, the set of measures that we present today is comprehensive, but by no means exhaustive. The new Sustainability dimension will continue to evolve over time, just as we do with the other pillars of the Agenda BC#. In addition, the challenges to the financial system brought about by climate change demand a coordinated and global action. Our growing interaction with other central banks and international organizations, as well as the frequent dialogue with financial institutions, are important to determine the evolution of our policies to minimize the effects of climate risks on our economy and financial system. Such interactions allow for the exchange of experiences and best practices, deepening our understanding of the risks associated with climate change. Striving for this integrated, coordinated and global approach, besides presenting more details of the BCBs agenda, in our event today we have guest-speakers from both the global and the Brazilian financial sectors, to underscore the importance of the issue at hand and to discuss the responses to the new challenges we face. We have a full agenda ahead of us, so let's continue with our event. We will start with the participation of our speakers, and in sequence, we will have a presentation by Governor Roberto Campos Neto and Deputy Governors, detailing the new Sustainability Dimension of the Agenda BC#. 3

Title: The global economic and monetary policy outlook
Subtitle: UBS High-level macro event
text: Apontamentos do presidente do Banco Central do Brasil Roberto Campos Neto UBS High-level macro event The global economic and monetary policy outlook Zurique (Suica), 2 de julho de 2019. Economic outlook Global economy The global outlook has been challenging for the EMEs, although becoming less so in the recent months, owing it to changes in the prospects for monetary policy in major economies. o Major central banks clearly indicated a willingness to provide additional monetary stimuli in case of need, which has contributed to easing global financial conditions. Nevertheless, the risks associated with a slowdown in global growth remain. o We judge that the risks associated with a slowing global economy remain and that economic policy and geopolitical may contribute to an even lower global growth. o In light of evidence of economic slowdown in several countries, the global environment may be more relevant to the dynamics of economic activity than previously anticipated. Macroeconomic conditions across EMEs are heterogeneous. o Institutions in EMEs are still under construction. It means that central banks in EMEs need to constantly foster credibility and that fiscal policy is often under scrutiny and exposed to stress risks. o Supply shocks are also stronger and sudden stops more frequent, resulting in higher FX, inflation and GDP volatility. o However, the macroeconomic conditions (fundamentals, buffers, policy stance etc) vary among EMEs, and some countries are more exposed or sensitive to movements in international financial markets. Policy makers must be vigilant with global economy developments, but, due to our buffers, Brazil is currently better prepared to withstand a setback in the international scenario. We count on: o A solid domestic financial system; o A robust balance of payment position (FDI around 5.2% of GDP, almost seven times the current account deficit); o A floating exchange rate regime; o An adequate level of international reserves (around 20% of GDP); o A low inflation and a well-anchored scenario of inflation expectations; Pagina 2 de 5 o Prospects of future structural reforms; and o Resumption of economic recovery ahead. Domestic economy In the domestic economy, recent data on economic activity indicate a halt in the process of economic recovery in the past quarters, but our baseline scenario assumes resumption of this process ahead, in a gradual fashion. o To a large extent, the effects on economic activity of the main shocks suffered by the Brazilian economy throughout 2018 have already dissipated. o In addition, financial conditions  which had tightened significantlybetween the second and fourth quarters of 2018  have already moved into more stimulative territory. There are risks around this baseline scenario in both directions. o On the one hand, (i) the high level of economic slack may continue to produce lower-thanexpected prospective inflation trajectory. o On the other hand, (ii) a possible frustration of expectations regarding the continuation of reforms and necessary adjustments in the Brazilian economy may affect risk premia and increase inflation over the relevant horizon for the conduct of monetary policy. Risk (ii) intensifies in case (iii) the global outlook for emerging economies deteriorates. o Although the balance of risks has evolved favorably, risk (ii) prevails at this time. Reforms Brazil falls behind the average of the AEs in the progress of structural reforms that support free market outcomes, although they have potentially high impacts on productivity and long-term growth. Fiscal sustainability is fundamental to reduce uncertainties, to increase confidence and investment, and consequently to foster long-term economic growth. o The advancement of structural reforms, in particular the public pension reform, is necessary. An acceleration of the pace of recovery of the economy to more robust levels will also depend on other initiatives aimed at productivity increases, efficiency gains, greater flexibility of the economy, and improvements in the business environment. Pagina 3 de 5 A recent IMF study1 shows that we have work to do in many dimension, such as: o Labour and products markets; o Legal system; and o Trade openess. In addition to that, there are reforms to be conducted in the banking sector. o In fact, among those, banking sector reforms are estimated to have the largest impact on productivity growth. Further, banking sector reforms are those that have more support among the population. In this regard, the BCB has a lot to contribute, and we are doing so through the Agenda BC#. Agenda BC# Agenda BC# adopts as principle a broad process financial democratization, freeing the markets from the need to finance the Government and opening up space for private entrepreneurship. We aim at simplifying savings instruments and democratizing access to them, regardless of the national origin of funds or whether they come from small or large investors. For that, we consider that technological evolution is crucial and our work has been organized along four dimensions: o Inclusion: to give simple access to markets for all investors  domestic and foreign, large and small; o Competitiveness: improve price formation through instruments of competitive access to markets; o Transparency: enhance the provision of information from the market and about the actions of the Central Bank. o Financial education: to promote the market participation of all types of agents, and to foster a culture of savings. Agenda BC# - Main actions This is being achieved through many working groups. To give a few examples: o Capital markets: Creating a regulatory sandbox; Improving instruments to use real estate as loan collateral (e.g.; reverse mortgage); 1 Brazil: boom, bust and road to recovery; Spilimbergo, Antonio & Srinivasan, Krishna; International Monetary Fund, June 2019. Pagina 4 de 5 Fostering the provision of FX hedge by the financial markets; Allowing the issuing of foreign currency debt in the domestic market by non-financial corporations; o Instant payments: we have already started a set of measures to create a system of instant payments in Brazil. o Open Banking: studies for the development of an open banking model for Brazil and discussions with markets participants are progressing. We expect to have concrete results on the coming months; Another important initiative is the movement towards full convertibility of the Real. The general objective here is to: o simplify bureaucracy; and o reduce costs for foreign capital to access the Brazilian market. These changes are expected to: o facilitate FX operations involving both capital flows and trade; o reduce costs to foreign investors; o increase local market liquidity and depth, helping to reduce markets volatility; and o turn the Real into a potential reference currency for the South America in the near future. Ending We must focus on the design of the financial system of the future. Without forgetting our missions of ensuring price stability and a solid and efficient financial system, it is important to be prepared for a technological and inclusive future. Pagina 5 de 5

Title: Economic outlook, monetary policy and the role of the BCB - Roadshow USA
Subtitle: Notes by the President of the Central Bank of Brazil, Robert Campos Neto at events on the trip to the US
text: Estados Unidos, de 10 a 14 de abril de 2019. Apontamentos do Presidente do Banco Central do Brasil, Roberto Campos Neto, em eventos na viagem aos Estados Unidos  Thank you for the invitation and for this opportunity to present our view on the progress in the economic outlook, the monetary policy and the role of the Central Bank of Brazil. I will also talk about some of the new priorities of the Agenda BC, our agenda of reforms for the Brazilian financial system. ---------- Global outlook  Regarding the global economy, the outlook remains challenging.  On the one hand, the risks associated with a slowdown in global growth, as a result of several uncertainties, are more elevated. Although the more positive outlook for the resolution of trade disputes may provide some support for the resumption of growth, the global economic slowdown has been more evident, with recent indicators confirming the moderation in economic activity and the reduction of agents confidence.  On the other hand, the risks associated with normalization of interest rates in some advanced economies have receded. With the balance of risks for economic activity substantially altered downwards, the main central banks reassessed their intentions to adjust interest rates in 2019, lengthening the process of monetary normalization.  Despite these uncertainties, the Brazilian economy has the capacity to withstand a setback in the international scenario, given its robust balance of payments, anchored inflation expectations, and prospects of economic recovery. Domestic outlook Inflation and economic activity  The Brazilian economy has suffered different shocks in 2018. The firm and transparent conduct of the Central Bank in the moments of higher volatility throughout 2018 was Pagina 2 de 11 fundamental to maintain the functionality of our markets and cushioned the impacts of these shocks on prices, which allowed: the consolidation of inflation around the target and the anchoring of inflation expectations; the consolidation of interest rates at historical lows; and the continuity of the process of gradual economic recovery.  Over the last few years, we have done the important task of reducing inflation, which had reached 10.7% in 2015 and, in the last 12 months, stands at 3.89%.  Various measures of underlying inflation are running at appropriate or comfortable levels. This includes the components that are most sensitive to the business cycle and monetary policy.  The inflation projections are around the targets: In the scenario with interest rate and exchange rate paths extracted from the Focus survey, the projections stand around 3.9% for 2019 and 3.8% for 2020. In the scenario with a constant Selic rate at 6.50% p.a., and a constant exchange rate at R3.85/US, inflation projections stand around 4.1% for 2019, and 4.0% for 2020.  The consolidation of inflation around the target and the anchoring of inflation expectations allowed the consistent reduction of the policy interest rate. The reductions brought the Selic rate from 14.25% in October 2016 to 6.5% currently, its historical low.  The current cycle of monetary easing has led to the fall in real interest rates (nominal interest rate minus inflation rate). These real rates, estimated using various measures, are currently close to 2.5% per year, which tends to stimulate the economy.  Regarding economic activity, the various shocks that affected the Brazilian economy in 2018 produced effects that persist even after their direct effects cease. Pagina 3 de 11  Recent data on economic activity came in below expectations. Nevertheless, the Brazilian economy remains on a gradual recovery path. In the last quarter of 2018, seasonally adjusted GDP grew 0.1% compared with the previous quarter. In 2018, GDP increased 1.1%, the same growth of 2017.  The lower activity growth in the last quarter of 2018 contributed to reduce the projection for 2019 GDP growth from 2.4% to 2.0%, as presented in the last edition of the Quarterly Inflation Report, of March 2019. Monetary policy  It is important to maintain the recent gains achieved in the conduct of monetary policy, which have been based on caution, serenity and perseverance.  At its last meeting, in March, the Copom unanimously decided to maintain the Selic rate at its historical low of 6.50% per year.  The baseline scenario for inflation involves risks in both directions. On the one hand, the high level of economic slack may lead to a lower-thanexpected prospective inflation trajectory. On the other hand, frustration of expectations regarding the continuation of reforms and necessary adjustments in the Brazilian economy may affect risk premia and increase the path for inflation over the relevant horizon for the conduct of monetary policy. This risk intensifies in case the global outlook for emerging economies deteriorates.  The balance of risks for inflation is symmetric.  The economic conditions with anchored inflation expectations, underlying inflation measures at appropriate or comfortable levels, inflation projected to move toward targets for 2019 and 2020, and high level of slack in the economy prescribe stimulative monetary policy, i.e., interest rates below the structural interest rate level. Pagina 4 de 11  The appropriate level of stimulus depends on the outlook conditions, particularly inflation expectations, the level of slack in the economy, the balance of risks and inflation projections.  It is important to observe how the Brazilian economy will behave over time, with lower uncertainty and without the effects of the various shocks that hit the economy last year. This assessment takes time and should not be completed in the short run.  The next steps in the conduct of monetary policy will continue to depend on the evolution of economic activity, the balance of risks, and on inflation projections and expectations.  Caution, serenity, and perseverance in monetary policy decisions, even in the face of volatile scenarios, have been instrumental in pursuing our primary objective of keeping the inflation path towards the targets. Reforms and adjustments in the Brazilian economy  The approval and implementation of reforms  notably those of fiscal nature  and adjustments in the Brazilian economy are essential to maintain low inflation in the medium and long run, for the reduction of its structural interest rate, and for sustainable economic recovery.  It is also necessary to pursue the changes that allow the development of our capital market. In this regard, fiscal adjustment measures may also contribute. Placing the public accounts on a balanced path, through a fiscal adjustment and a patrimonial restructuring, generates multiplier effects on the capital market, resulting in a greater diversification of this market and an increase in the number of transactions.  Financial intermediation in Brazil has to free itself from the ties that hold it to the government. The market must free itself from the need to finance the government and turn to entrepreneurship financing.  We also believe that an autonomous central bank would be better prepared to consolidate the recent gains and to enable the improvements that the country needs. Pagina 5 de 11  We need to focus on the design of the financial system of the future, especially on the role of technological evolution. This innovation route has intensified in recent years with the increase of: Processing capacity; Information storage; Information organization; and The interpretation of information and the use of data. Without forgetting the missions of ensuring price stability and a solid and efficient financial system, it is important to prepare the Central Bank for a technological and inclusive future. Modernizing the Brazilian financial system is crucial to achieve these goals  simplifying and de-bureaucratizing the access to financial markets for all agents and giving homogeneous treatment to capital regardless of nationality or whether it comes from a large or small investor.  For the financial system, this technological change means: Democratize; Digitalize; De-bureaucratize; and Demonetize.  We need to master the tools to create this future: Blockchain; cloud services; artificial intelligence; and digitalization.  I am convinced that with all of our efforts, the Central Bank of Brazil will contribute to the design of a better country, based on the free market. Future of the Agenda BC  The Central Bank of Brazil is promoting a structural reform agenda for the financial system, the Agenda BC. This is a dynamic, permanently improved agenda, whose actions, conducted in a synergistic and integrated manner, help the Central Bank to fulfill its mission of Pagina 6 de 11 ensuring the stability of the currencys purchasing power and a solid and efficient financial system. To date, the Central Bank has completed 41 actions of the Agenda BC. 19 actions were concluded in 2016 and 2017. 22 actions were concluded in 2018. It is necessary to deepen the Agenda BC in order to promote a broad process of financial democratization. This democratization is necessary to expand the provision of resources to the productive sector in fair conditions, and generate benefits for all Brazilians. Until now, the financial democratization has focused on assuring access to payment services and the credit market. Let us move forward in other dimensions, with a special focus on the capital market. We need to remove distortions and implement policies to improve the efficiency of our markets. The Agenda BC is now being re-evaluated and expanded. It will include new dimensions: Inclusion: to facilitate access to the market for investors and borrowers, domestic and foreign, large and small. Competitiveness: to promote adequate pricing through instruments of competitive access to markets. Transparency: to improve transparency in the process of price formation and in information from the market and the Central Bank. Financial education: to promote the participation of all type of agents in the financial market, and a culture of saving. Within these new dimensions, 14 working groups are being created to evaluate more closely each topic. Pagina 7 de 11 These dimensions will be worked through actions with other government bodies and the society, as well as bills of law and changes in regulation, always with a view to: Democratize; Digitalize; De-bureaucratize; and Demonetize. The working groups are dealing with the following topics: In the Inclusion dimension: Microcredit: to increase the importance and the diffusion of microcredit in the market. Cooperativism: to expand cooperativism in areas with low banking penetration, pursuing digital solutions. Capital market: to promote changes that allow the full development of our capital market, based on the free market.  The changes in this area have already begun. The TLP and the change in BNDESs focus have shown that, when the government reduces, opening space in the market, private initiative flourishes.  The literature shows a clear positive correlation between the size of capital market and economic growth. Thus, it is crucial to move ahead. Convertibility: to simplify rules, reduce bureaucracy and facilitate operations in the FX market, in order to permit that eventually the Brazilian Real becomes a convertible currency that is a reference in the region. In the Competitiveness dimension: Innovations: o Instant payments: important mechanism to democratize the means of payments. It involves a set of measures to create a system of instant payments in Brazil. o Open Banking: studies for the development of an open banking model for Brazil. The aim is to reduce entry barriers and increase competition. Pagina 8 de 11 o Guarantees: development of guarantee centers operating as mechanisms to diversify risks and provide means to reduce market volatility. o Cyber-security: this is a point of attention and risk in an increasingly digitized financial system. It is necessary to set up an effective cybersecurity policy and to develop defense and risk minimization mechanisms. International reserves: studies on the return and management of international reserves, and intervention instruments. In the Transparency dimension: Rural credit: studies on a new financing model for rural activity. The objective is to increase the efficiency of subsidies, focusing on small and medium rural producers. To do so, it is necessary to make explicit the implicit subsidies and better evaluate their destinations. Real estate market: modernize the mechanisms used to raise funds for civil construction, improving housing financing, allowing transparency on subsidies and widening the options available to households and firms. Relationship with Congress: strengthen the relationship with Congress and study ways to make objectives and progresses measurable. Relationship with major investors: develop mechanisms to improve the relationship of the Brazilian government with large portfolio investors. Improve information on financial services and products, including compliance costs. Market Efficiency: enhance the efficiency in the market area of the Central Bank, generating synergies and expanding the flow of information. Communication plan for the Central Bank actions: improve communication of our actions and maintain frequent contact with the media and the public, publicizing our initiatives and actions. Pagina 9 de 11 Transparency and communication: develop objective and quantifiable methods to measure the efficacy of our communication. In the Financial Education dimension: Financial education: to create programs to stimulate financial education, through the deepening of actions with market and government institutions, and using cooperatives and microcredit entities as dissemination agents.  The objectives of each of these working groups are complex, and to follow the progress of these initiatives the Central Bank is creating monitoring indexes that allow us to measure and establish clear objectives for: market capitalization with private sources; the diffusion of microcredit and cooperativism among the target population of these programs; spending on bureaucracy in accessing our markets; the degree of financial intermediation in our markets; and the inclusion of different demographic groups in our financial markets. Final remarks  I would like to emphasize the main messages: The global outlook remains challenging. The domestic macroeconomic environment has been characterized by the following phenomena: Inflation around the target and anchored inflation expectations; Gradual process of economic recovery; Interest rates at historical lows. Pagina 10 de 11 The approval and implementation of reforms, especially those on the fiscal side, and adjustments in the Brazilian economy are crucial for the sustainability of the environment of low and stable inflation and for long-term growth. As regards the future, we will work to: Keep inflation low and stable, maintaining the excellent conduct of monetary policy, and continue to improve our communication; Keep the financial system solid and efficient, with a larger and more democratic capital market, with participation of more households and firms; Approve the legal autonomy of the Central Bank of Brazil, helping to reduce the country risk and rise the long-term growth; Reduce the cost of financial intermediation, increasing the efficiency of this service and enhancing competition; Make the financial markets more open to all types of agents: small and large, national and foreign. Pagina 11 de 11

Title: Speech - BCB Autonomy Law Enactment Ceremony - February 2021
Subtitle: Speech by Roberto Campos Neto Governor of Banco Central do Brasil
text: Brasilia - DF, February 24, 2021 Autonomy Law Enactment Ceremony Speech by Roberto Campos Neto Governor of Banco Central do Brasil Good evening everyone! I start by greeting all participants in this ceremony: The President of the Republic, Jair Bolsonaro The Minister of Economy, Paulo Guedes Other authorities present here. Today, with the enactment by the President of the Republic, Jair Bolsonaro, of the law that grants autonomy to the Central Bank, Brazil takes an important step. This Law represents an institutional milestone for our country. The idea of an autonomous Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) was already in place even before its creation. My grandfather  Roberto Campos, Minister of Planning during the presidents Castello Branco administration and one of the main authorities behind the creation of the BCB  was a great advocate of the institution's autonomy. Enacted in December 1964, Law No. 4,595 created the BCB with formal autonomy, by establishing that the BCBs Governor and Deputy Governors had a fixed-term mandate of six years, a term greater than that of the President of the Republic at the time, of five years. However, such autonomy was short-lived, disappearing as early as 1967, with the replacement of the first BCBs governor before the end of his term. Speech on Autonomy Law Enactment (Supplementary Law No. 179/2021) - February 2021 It would take more than 50 years for a confluence of factors to restore the BCB's formal autonomy. In this context, I would like to thank the President of the Republic, Jair Bolsonaro; the Minister of Economy, Paulo Guedes; and the National Congress, as represented here by the presidents of the House of Representatives and the Senate. This milestone is also the result of a long process of institutional development and also derive from the efforts of previous BCBs Boards, as well as on the BCBs staff, to whom I also express my appreciation. Throughout this process, the benefits of an autonomous, transparent, and accountable central bank have become clearer to our society. Economic literature and international experience show that central bank autonomy is associated with lower and less volatile inflation, without compromising economic growth. A high inflation environment is especially costly for the low-income population, which has limited access to financial instruments to protect their earnings from inflation or has more limited financial education. The inflation targeting system along with a legally autonomous BCBs decision-making are imperative to ensure that these citizens are protected against the damages inflicted by high inflation. Moreover, the literature also shows that an autonomous central bank can better guarantee the stability of the financial system. In Brazil, the approval of a legal framework granting the BCBs formal operational autonomy will provide greater confidence that the Institution will be able to fulfill its objectives. The increase in BCB credibility built upon the legal autonomy will allow for lower structural interest rates, lower risks and a more stable monetary policy. In other words, this institutional change will benefit the whole society. The Law states that, price stability remains the BCBs primary objective. Without compromising the fulfillment of its main objective, the BCB should also aim to ensure the stability and efficiency of the financial system, smooth out fluctuations in economic activity, and promote full employment. Central bank autonomy can encompass three dimensions: operational, administrative, and financial. The BCB's operational autonomy, granted by the legislation enacted today, entails the freedom to use the instruments to fulfill the objectives established by the National Monetary Council (CMN). Speech on Autonomy Law Enactment (Supplementary Law No. 179/2021) - February 2021 The changes brought about by the Law establish a new institutional framework that reinforces an important balance of powers. The Law sets four-year terms for Board members that do not coincide with those of the President of the Republic. This isolates the monetary policy cycle from the shorter political cycle. The Law also guarantees that the President of the Republic chooses all Board members at a staggered manner. Therefore, some Board members, nominated during the prior administration will retain their positions during governmental transitions, thus creating a cycle of continuity. Finally, the Brazilian Congress remains responsible for evaluating and approving the presidents nominations for Governor and Deputy Governors. Therefore, the autonomy inherent to this balance of powers does not mean complete freedom. In addition, the legal autonomy requires greater transparency, assured through a set of instruments: The BCBs Governor must carry out public Senate hearings, in the first and second semesters of each year, presenting the Inflation Report and the Financial Stability Report and explaining the decisions taken in the previous semester; Statements and minutes of the meetings of the Monetary Policy Committee (Copom) and the Financial Stability Committee (Comef) must be published periodically; and The BCBs Governor must participate in public hearings with purpose of accountability to authorities and society. Ladies and gentlemen, the institutional enhancement brought about by the legal autonomy of the Banco Central do Brasil will contribute to consolidate the gains achieved in recent years in terms of price stability and financial stability. Legal autonomy also complements and supports the broad reform agenda undertaken by BCB to promote a more efficient, competitive and inclusive financial system in Brazil. Thank you very much. Speech on Autonomy Law Enactment (Supplementary Law No. 179/2021) - February 2021

Title: Speech by Mr. Diogo Abry Guillen at the Economic Affairs Committee (CAE) of the Federal Senate. - 135.2 Kb
text: The CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL Brasilia, April 5, 2022. Statement by Mr. Diogo Abry Guillen at the Hearing of the Committee on Economic Affairs (CAE) of the Federal Senate for consideration of his nomination to the position of Director of the Central Bank of Brazil Your Excellency Senator Otto Alencar, Chairman of the Committee on Economic Affairs; Your Excellency Senator Espiridiao Amin, Rapporteur of the process that deals with the nomination of my name as Director of the Central Bank of Brazil; Honourable Senators and Honourable Senators; other authorities present, press professionals and those who watch us on Senate TV, ladies and gentlemen, good morning. It is with great honor and satisfaction that I appear before this Commission as a nominee for the position of Director of the Central Bank of Brazil. I thank the President of the Central Bank of Brazil for forwarding my name and His Excellency the President of the Republic for the honor granted by indicating my name for the consideration of this House. I believe it is relevant, in view of such an honor, to make some brief comments about my trajectory and my perspective of the Central Bank's mission for the evaluation of this House. I reinforce, from now on, my unconditional effort and commitment to the best use of my academic and professional experiences in order to conduct economic policy in line with the mission and objectives of the Central Bank of Brazil. My academic career began twenty years ago when I was studying for an undergraduate degree in Economic Sciences at PUC-Rio. Since then, macroeconomics and macrointernational have aroused my interest, both from an academic point of view and from the point of view linked to public policies and conjunctural understanding. Another area of academic interest, related to monetary policy topics, was maintained during the master's course, when I specialized in topics related to price formation and inflation expectations, including later publications. After finishing my master's degree, I studied for a doctorate at Princeton University, studying topics related to the optimal conduct of monetary policy, price formation, and the understanding of financial and economic relations between countries. Despite the academic plunge, the interest in the more conjunctural economy and linked to the economic policies applied remained throughout this period. During my doctorate, I had the opportunity to work, for a few months, at the Central Bank of Belgium and at the Federal Reserve - Minneapolis, United States, living with some researchers who are references in the construction of macroeconomic models used by central banks of several countries, in addition to better understanding empirical aspects in price formation. At the end of my doctorate, I chose to return to Brazil and work in the financial market, where I improved my understanding and economic monitoring techniques, building scenarios and projections for several countries, including the United States and several emerging countries. Concomitant with my work in the financial market, I taught in the Master's Degree in Macroeconomics and Finance at PUC-Rio, offering courses in Empirical Macroeconomics and International Finance, in addition to advising or co-advising students in the academic, professional and doctoral master's degrees. Most of the dissertations and theses dealt with topics of monetary policy, international macroeconomics or empirical methods for forecasting economic series. In 2015, I transferred to Itau Asset Management, where I recently served as Chief Economist, leading the institution's macroeconomic research, quantitative research and data science teams. Concomitant with my work at Itau Asset, I became a professor of the master's and doctoral programs at Insper, again offering courses in Monetary Economics and International Finance, in addition to advising several master's and doctoral students, with theses and dissertations presented at national and international conferences. This is the set of skills and experiences that I intend to add to those already existing in the Collegiate Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Brazil with the objective of contributing to the fulfillment of the important mission of ensuring the stability of the purchasing power of the currency, ensure a solid, efficient and competitive financial system, and foster the economic well-being of society. If I receive the vote of confidence from this valuable Commission and my nomination is confirmed by the plenary of the Federal Senate, I have no doubt that my academic and professional experience can be added to the excellent work of the Central Bank of Brazil. Before closing, I would like to make a few comments about the mission of the Central Bank of Brazil. The achievement of low and stable inflation over time, according to the target and intervals established by the National Monetary Council, following the inflation targeting regime, is part of the Central Bank's mission and its fundamental objective. Maintaining low inflation over time requires constant and attentive monitoring, associated with effective communication, for better decision-making. Only with this posture will we keep inflation low and stable and reduce the future risks of inflation, also providing a structural reduction in the interest rate; contributing, in a relevant way, to the economic well-being of society, smoothing fluctuations in the level of economic activity and fostering full employment. Regarding the financial system, the Central Bank must maintain, through regulation and supervision, the proper functioning of this system to ensure the efficient intermediation of resources, as well as properly manage and mitigate risks. A solid, efficient and competitive financial system is part of the Central Bank's agenda, as well as its mission. If Your Excellencies grant me the honor of approving my name for the position of Director of the Central Bank of Brazil, I assume, from now on, the commitment to offer all my knowledge and experience to work together with the other members of the Collegiate Board of Directors in the fulfillment of the institutional mission and objectives of the Central Bank. I thank you for your attention and I make myself available to Your Excellencies to answer any questions. Thank you very much!

Title: Remarks by the Director of Economic Policy, Diogo Abry Guillen, at the end of the first day of the Annual Conference of the Central Bank of Brazil. - 182.8 Kb
text: CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL Notes by the Director of Economic Policy and Director of Monetary Policy, Diogo Abry Guillen, in the Closing of the first day of the First Annual Conference of the Central Bank of Brazil Brasilia, 5/17/2023 Good afternoon everyone. It is with great satisfaction that we are holding the first edition of the Annual Conference of the Central Bank of Brazil, which is now an important forum for the exchange of experiences and knowledge, the dissemination of studies and relevant debates of interest to central banks. After three years without holding events, due to the pandemic, we decided to unify two of the most important meetings held by the Central Bank of Brazil: the Annual Seminar on Inflation Targeting, which began to be held in 1999, along with the implementation of the targeting regime in Brazil, and the Annual Seminar on Financial Stability and Banking Economics, started in 2005. The unification and transformation into the Annual Conference of the Central Bank strengthens the event, in addition to expanding the scope of debates and reinforcing the scope of the Central Bank's areas of activity. On this occasion, it is a source of pride to have the responsibility of uttering a few words in this closing act of the first day of the event and I would like to thank and congratulate all the teams involved in the organization and realization of this event. We know all the effort and dedication undertaken in this event. On behalf of the Central Bank of Brazil, I would also like to thank all those present and, in particular, the exhibitors, debaters and moderators who promptly accepted our invitation to participate in this Conference and are, without a doubt, an indispensable condition for the success of the event. It was an honor to have been able to count on the keynote speeches of Mrs. Gita Gopinath and Professor Robert Townsend today, as well as the presentations of our distinguished guests Amir Sufi, Elias Albagli, Sabine Mauderer and Stijn Claessens. speakers from different institutions. I feel honored to have participated in this edition, in the role of moderator, but also as an attentive listener. Ladies and Gentlemen, In addition to today, designed to promote discussions on current issues and their relationship with policymaking, we will also have two days dedicated to presentations of papers in academic format. We will have the participation of experts from various central banks, national academia, multilateral bodies and major research centers around the world. 37 papers will be presented, chosen from a total of 269 submitted articles, dealing with the areas of macroeconomics, sustainability, financial stability, banking economics, financial intermediation and innovation, macroprudential regulation, international economics and finance. My invitation to all those who can follow these sessions is registered. The past editions of the seminars, as well as the quality of the papers accepted for this Conference, excite us a lot for the coming days. At this point, I will comment on some of the important recent advances implemented by the Central Bank of Brazil in the field of transparency. A topic that is widely addressed both in the literature and in the practice of monetary policy refers to the gains of having an autonomous central bank, proven theoretically and empirically, achievement of the objectives set for central banks. The de jure autonomy of the Central Bank of Brazil and the overlapping mandates, established in Complementary Law 179, of February 24, 2021, provide greater predictability in the economy and prevent the conduct of monetary policy from being subject to non-technical injunctions. In fact, the autonomy of the Central Bank of Brazil is fundamental for economic stability in the country. Today, however, I would like to talk about the other side of the coin regarding autonomy, which is accountability. Intuitively, the basic idea is that, along with the delegation of the conduct of monetary policy, comes accountability. These two concepts are, in the end, two sides of the same coin and autonomy will be as strong as accountability and vice versa. On the one hand, the Central Bank is delegated the operational autonomy to meet the target established by the National Monetary Council. On the other hand, it is up to the Central Bank to explain to the different actors of the economy and to society in general how it has conducted its actions to achieve the objectives that have been delegated to it. Thus, the transparency of the Central Bank's decision-making process is fundamental to its legitimacy. In addition, transparency, by allowing a better understanding of the actions of the monetary authority and facilitating the coordination of expectations, also increases the effectiveness of monetary policy. And I must say that we have made important advances in transparency. We are using different platforms on social networks and using more accessible language, thus seeking to be up to date on communication trends and reach a wider audience. We are also increasing transparency in relation to the monetary policy decision-making process. First, the Central Bank understands that publishing its different models is It has been done, with the publication of updates to the models used in the monetary policy decision-making process, in boxes in the Inflation Report or in the Series of Papers for Discussion, with levels of greater detail than in the past. I would also like to highlight the greater detail of the Central Bank's analysis and projections system, with a description of the elements that make up the production of projections and scenarios and the entire process that supports monetary policy decisions. Such publications allow a better understanding of the decisions of the Monetary Policy Committee, based on technical foundations, following the best international practices in the use of modeling and economic analysis and, it is worth emphasizing, always with the valuable support of civil servants from different areas in this process. The Central Bank's greater transparency is also observed in monetary policy communication documents. In line with other central banks, press releases, minutes and reports also began to transparently reflect the decision-making process. The discussion of alternative scenarios, hypotheses, concerns and divergences contributes to the understanding of the decision-making process. However, part of this communication is very technical and is restricted to a more specialized audience. Notably, recent literature has emphasized the need for a citizen language to reach society in general. Thus, seeking to fill this gap, it is worth mentioning the creation and publication, in March of this year, of the Visual Summary in the Inflation Report, which seeks to bring, in a synthetic way, the main messages of the Report, accompanied by representative images. Finally, the Central Bank has also sought to increase the transparency of the research it develops in the different fields of activity. Research in the Central Bank plays a role banking efficiency, providing high-quality results, economic models and analytical tools used in policy decisions, which allow a better understanding of important issues in the Brazilian and global economies. In this sense, in December 2021, we published the BC Research Agenda, which seeks to guide the research developed at the Institution, based on its institutional mission, its strategic objectives, and the challenges brought by new technologies. The main results of the research activities are disseminated and disseminated on the Institution's website, especially in the Series of Papers for Discussion, which has almost 600 papers published, and in the Research Report on Economics and Finance, whose edition for 2022 has just been published. In addition, also with the objective of bringing communication closer to society, we will soon launch, on the Central Bank's website, the research blog, whose objective is to be a channel for the dissemination of studies in the various areas of the Central Bank to society. The posts, which will identify the authors, will cover a wide range of topics, presented in different styles and approaches. The fundamental commitment of the blog is to make the texts be disseminated in a language that is more accessible to the general public. In addition, a page will be launched with the profiles of civil servants who develop research at the Central Bank with information about their research areas and listing the published and developing works. Such innovations complement the means in which we disseminate a rich and lively research agenda, which contributes so much to the evolution of the Central Bank. Accountability involves not only being transparent about what you do, but seeking the best way to transmit this information, reaching different audiences. The Bank has advanced in this aspect and will continue to advance in this direction in the future. Moving on to the final words, I want to remind you that, next year, we will complete 30 years of monetary stability, brought about by the Real Plan, and 25 years of the inflation targeting regime in Brazil, which consolidated the monetary stability of our currency. After having gone through a past of economic instability due to uncontrolled inflation, we are proud of this achievement, which is the result of the maturation of Brazilian society and which was accompanied by the improvement of our institutions. We must not forget that maintaining price stability is essential so that Brazil no longer goes through the difficulties associated with uncontrolled prices. High inflation disorganizes society and disrupts the functioning of the country's productive structure, generating enormous inefficiencies, harming economic growth and penalizing mainly the less favored layers of the population. Low and stable inflation allows people to make more informed and secure decisions about consumption, investment, and savings, increasing the efficiency of the economy, favoring its growth, and preventing the lowest-income population and the least assisted from being negatively impacted by higher inflation. In fact, low inflation is a social good. Thus, keeping the inflation rate low, stable and predictable is the best contribution of the Central Bank's monetary policy so that the country can grow sustainably with job creation and ensuring the maintenance of the purchasing power of Brazilians. possible cost, the control of inflation and the sustainable growth of the economy. The credibility of the Central Bank of Brazil and the inflation targeting regime are achievements of the whole society. Ladies and gentlemen, Looking ahead and recognizing the challenges to be faced, I must affirm that the Central Bank of Brazil will continue to base its actions on the experience and responsibility of its directors and, mainly, on the institutional commitment and recognized technical quality of its staff. Finally, I would like to take this opportunity to invite everyone to the second edition of the Annual Conference of the Central Bank of Brazil, to be held next year. We count, once again, on the relevant and essential contribution of all, whether through the submission of papers or through participation in the debates, so that next year's event continues to be special like this one. Thank you.

Em nome do Banco Central do Brasil, tambm agradeo a todos os presentes e, em especial, aos expositores, debatedores e moderadores que prontamente aceitaram nosso convite para participar desta Conferncia e so, sem dvida, condio indispensvel para o sucesso do evento. Gita Gopinath e do Professor Robert Townsend, bem como com as apresentaes de nossos ilustres convidados Amir Sufi, Elias Albagli, Sabine Mauderer e Stijn Claessens. A autonomia de Jure do Banco Central do Brasil e os mandatos superpostos, estabelecidos na Lei Complementar 179, de 24 de fevereiro de 2021, proporcionam maior previsibilidade na economia e evitam que a conduo da poltica monetria fique sujeita a injunes no tcnicas. De fato, a autonomia do Banco Central do Brasil  fundamental para a estabilidade econmica no pas. Hoje, no entanto, gostaria de falar sobre o outro lado da moeda referente  autonomia, que  a prestao de contas. De forma intuitiva, a ideia bsica  que, junto com a delegao da conduo da poltica monetria, vem a prestao de contas. Assim, a transparncia do processo decisrio do Banco Central  fundamental para sua legitimidade. Alm disso, a transparncia, ao permitir melhor entendimento das aes da autoridade monetria e facilitar a coordenao das expectativas, tambm aumenta a efetividade da poltica monetria. E devo dizer que temos feito importantes avanos na transparncia. Tambm estamos ampliando a transparncia em relao ao processo decisrio de poltica monetria. Em primeiro lugar, o BC entende que publicar seus diferentes modelos  Pgina 4 de 8 sido feito, com publicaes das atualizaes dos modelos utilizados no processo decisrio de poltica monetria, em boxes no Relatrio de Inflao ou na Srie de Trabalhos para Discusso, com nveis de detalhamento maior do que no passado. Destaco tambm o maior detalhamento do sistema de anlise e projees do Banco Central, com a descrio dos elementos que compem a produo de projees e cenrios e de todo o processo que d suporte s decises de poltica monetria. Por fim, o Banco Central tambm tem buscado aumentar a transparncia da pesquisa que desenvolve nos diferentes campos de atuao. Alm disso, tambm com o objetivo de tornar a comunicao mais prxima da sociedade, lanaremos em breve, no site do Banco Central, o blog de pesquisa, cujo objetivo  ser um canal de divulgao de estudos das diversas reas do BC para a sociedade. As postagens, que identificaro os autores, cobriro ampla gama de temas, apresentados em diferentes estilos e abordagens. Alm disso, ser lanada uma pgina com os perfis dos servidores que desenvolvem pesquisas no BC com informaes sobre suas reas de pesquisa e listando os trabalhos publicados e em desenvolvimento. A prestao de contas envolve no s ser transparente sobre o que se faz, mas buscar a melhor forma de transmitir essa informao, atingindo os diferentes pblicos. O Banco Pgina 6 de 8 centrais, tem avanado nesse aspecto e seguir avanando nesta direo no futuro. J caminhando para as palavras finais, quero lembrar que, no prximo ano, completaremos 30 anos da estabilidade monetria, trazida pelo Plano Real, e 25 anos do regime de metas para a inflao no Brasil, que consolidou a estabilidade monetria de nossa moeda. Depois de termos percorrido um passado de instabilidade econmica por descontrole inflacionrio, temos orgulho dessa conquista, que  resultado do amadurecimento da sociedade brasileira e que foi acompanhada pelo aprimoramento de nossas instituies. Dessa forma, manter a taxa de inflao baixa, estvel e previsvel  a melhor contribuio da poltica monetria do Banco Central para que o pas possa crescer de forma sustentvel com gerao de empregos e garantindo a manuteno do poder de compra dos brasileiros. Pgina 7 de 8 custo possvel, o controle da inflao e o crescimento sustentvel da economia. Senhoras e senhores, Olhando para a frente e reconhecendo os desafios a serem enfrentados, devo afirmar que o Banco Central do Brasil continuar pautando suas aes na experincia e responsabilidade de seus dirigentes e, principalmente, no comprometimento institucional e na reconhecida qualidade tcnica de seu corpo funcional. Title: Comments by Director Fernanda Guardado at the Web Talk: Sustainable Finance: From Pledges to Progress, promoted by the German Agency for International Cooperation (GIZ).
text: Sustainable Finance: From Pledges to Progress - October 20th, 2022 Fernanda Guardado, Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Brazil Good afternoon, Ute. Good afternoon Jochen, Marjeta, Tanja and all colleagues present on this panel. It is a pleasure to be with you today and talk not only about sustainability, but also to have a chance to highlight the importance of having the GIZ as a close partner of the Central Bank of Brazil (BCB). It is widely known that tackling climate and environmental risks and the massive challenges that come with them demands close dialogue and a global answer. Values such as information sharing, coordination, and the promotion of a better understanding on environmental and climate related issues are highly welcome, and it is precisely at this point that the GIZ has helped us so much. The Central Bank of Brazil is one of the global leaders in sustainable central banking. What has been the motivation for the Central Bank to push sustainability so vigorously? Let me start by talking a bit about the BCBs involvement with matters related to sustainability. Although it is important to highlight that the Central Banks history in this agenda goes back some time, with some well-received regulations in the past. Today this issues have gained further importance, and there is widespread recognition of the need to rethink the relationship with the environment from different perspectives, especially in the economy and the financial system. The BCB has been following closely the rapid evolution of the environmental and climate agenda worldwide. It is worth mentioning the launching, in September 2020, of the Sustainability Dimension of the BCBs Strategic Agenda, known as Agenda BC#. This marks the recognition of the relevance of these issues for the Pagina 1 de 7 BCBs operations and strategies. In general terms, we can consider that the Central Bank of Brazil brought social, environmental, and climate-related variables to several of its decision-making processes, regardless of their complexity. Having in mind that the BCBs objectives are to ensure price stability and the strength, soundness, and efficiency of the National Financial System, and since extreme climate events that were previously considered uncommon have become more frequent, it became clear that we had the need to dwell further into climate and environmental related risks. As policy makers and regulators, we needed to better acess the impacts of these events on main economic variables in the relevant horizon for monetary policy, as well as issues related to the soundness of the financial system, such as loans collaterals and physical assets value, among others, under. Where do you see the greatest risks and opportunities with respect to sustainable finance in Brazil? In order to embrace not only risks, but also the great opportunities than come with this agenda, the BCB established in 2020 a set of concrete measures and objectives spread into five main pillars: regulation; supervision; development of policies and instruments; establishment of partnerships; and internal actions. Since 2021, the BCB disclosed a series of new regulations, which include:  CMN Resolution 4,943, altering Resolution 4,557/17 to include a specific section on the management of social, environmental, and climate-related risks applied to financial institutions in Segments 1-4.  CMN Resolution 4,944, altering Resolution 4,557/17 to include a specific section on the management of social, environmental, and climate-related risks applied to financial institutions of Segment 5. These new risks will start to be published next year. Pagina 2 de 7  CMN Resolution 4,945, revoking Resolution 4,327/14, to establish new requirements for financial institutions (Segments 1-5) relative to a new Social, Environmental and Climate Responsibility Policy.  Resolution BCB 140, which establishes the Green Rural Credit Bureau, providing for the characterization of enterprises with restrictions on access to rural credit due to legal or infra-legal provisions relating to social, environmental, and climate-related issues. One of the expected results of the Green Credit Bureau is, by bringing more information and transparency to the rural credit system, to foster the conditions for a greener agriculture.  BCB Resolution No. 204, of March 22, 2022 - which provides for the sharing of data on operations registered in the Rural Credit and Proagro Operations System (Sicor). This Resolution establishes an open finance approach towards rural credit operations, allowing borrowers of this type of credit to share, with whomever they wish, information regarding their rural credit operations registered with Sicor. As a result, the BCB aims to: (i) make better use of Sicor as a valuable repository of data that can be used by the financial and capital markets, as well as by rural producers for the efficient allocation of resources; (ii) allow rural producers to bring greater transparency regarding their level of leverage in rural credit operations, especially for potential financing agents that are not FIs; and (iii) contribute to the offer of financing in better conditions for rural producers, according to the effective risk of their operations and, consequently, to reduce the level of indebtedness of this segment as a whole, inside and outside the National Financial System. This measure will add to the Green Bureau of Rural Credit, which aims to mitigate data gaps and foster a greener rural activity in Brazil.  CMN Resolution No. 4,968, of November 25, 2021 - which establishes that financial institutions internal control systems must provide, among other aspects, controls that aim to avoid the institution's involvement in improper or illegal activities, especially those related to social, environmental and climate risks. Pagina 3 de 7 Another important aspect to highlight was the incorporation of Taskforce on Climate-related Financial Disclosure (TCFD) recommendations in the prudential framework of financial institutions. Given the complexity of the recommendations the BCB opted for a gradual adoption, with implementation in two phases:  Phase 1: concluded in September 2021, with the publication of regulation, in which qualitative aspects are addressed, with a focus on governance, institutional strategy and the management of risk; and  Phase 2: ongoing in the next months, with the incorporation of quantitative aspects, focusing on metrics, goals and measuring climate-related risks. The publication of the first Report on Social, Environmental and Climate-Related Risks in September 2021 was another important milestone. Not only does the document address BCBs sustainability actions in an integrated way, but it also strengthens the communication on the set of rules, practices, and projects of the BCB that have the objective of the better management of social, environmental, and climate-related risks, both internally and within the National Financial System. The Report is aligned with the recommendations published by the World Economic Forum (WEF), the TCFD and the NGFS. This regular report will allow the BCB to remain at the forefront of this important topic and to increase its transparency and accountability. It is also important to highlight that the BCB is concluding its work towards publishing the first climate risk evaluation exercise for the National Financial System in the next Financial Stability Report, to be release on November 3rd, 2022. The exercise will be made up of two parts: the first one will be a mapping of credit exposure according to the transition risk of the borrower; and the second will be a sensitivity analysis that will be focused on physical risk related to extreme droughts, using the climate scenarios developed by the National Institute for Space Research - INPE. In this analysis, the BCB will measure the banking systems credit exposure to this risk. The BCB has also some ongoing research projects on the Sustainability Dimension, such as the Effect of frost on the production chain of firms, which Pagina 4 de 7 aims to apply network econometric methods to infer the magnitude and propagation of local shocks using real-time data on payments, lending, and prices; and the Economic and financial effects of the Mariana disaster, which aims to measure the economic and financial effects of water contamination in riverside municipalities, including economic activity, payment flow in the production chain and local consumption; among other projects. To what extent do you think Brazils experience in sustainable finance could be used as role model for other countries to scale sustainable finance? As you can see, we had a very busy agenda in the last couple of years. In the first few months of the Sustainability Dimension, it can be said that the BCB worked tirelessly in a credibility gaining phase. It is known that the environmental discussion in Brazil is sensitive, and the eyes of the whole world are on us, so the Central Bank of Brazil has concentrated its efforts on concrete actions with very well-defined deadlines, in areas strongly connected to our specific mandate. After the first year of the Sustainability Dimension's anniversary, with the publication of several new regulations and reports in 2021, I believe that the perception of the BCB's objectives in relation to this agenda has become clearer. Having had great success towards risk management and disclosure-related initiatives, we now turn our eyes to fostering sustainable finance in Brazil. In this mission, we are working together with other regulators and Government bodies in Brazil to address the issues that hamper the increase in issuance of green and sustainability-linked bonds, such as the lack of a national taxonomy, as well as participate in the discussions surrounding a market for carbon credit. In this sense, one aspect that helps us and I think it could help other institutions as well is the fact that the BCB treats sustainability strategically. Since we want to be on the frontier of knowledge in this field and because we understand that this is a dynamic agenda, we can say that dealing with aspects related to climate and sustainability within the strategic planning of institutions helps a lot, especially with regard to the traction of measures and the engagement of your staff. So Pagina 5 de 7 working together and engaging all the interested parties, be it between the BCBs many departments or with other regulators, is an important lesson from our recent experience. What is your experience with the Central Bank and Supervisors Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) and its role to foster sustainable finance globally? It is impossible not to say a few words about the NGFS. I can say that, as the Central Bank of Brazil became a member of the NGFS in March 2020, their efforts and recommendations were great inspirations for the BCBs initiatives, just a few months afterwards, in September 2020. At that time, the NGFS had released important guides that were quite beneficial for all central banks, such as the Guide for Sustainable and Responsible Investment for Central Banks Portfolio Management and the Guide for Supervisors, which we had the pleasure to coordinate its review on 2021, published previously to the COP-26, named the Progress Report to the Guide for Supervisors. NGFS has been a reliable and trustworthy source not only of precious guides that help to bring some cohesion to practices between central banks, but also a generator of public goods such as their climate scenarios, which are used by both public and private entities to assess their exposure and risks to different scenarios. It has also helped to mobilize mainstream finance to support the transition toward a sustainable economy. In other words, we can say that it is difficult to talk nowadays about the role of central banks on the sustainability front without thinking about the NGFS. What is your experience of cooperating with Germany, specifically with GIZ? Where do you see further need or potential to expand the Brazilian- German cooperation in sustainable finance? In closing, I would like to thank deeply the GIZ for the close cooperation we have had in recent years. I believe that our joint projects have a very special feature in the development of this agenda, which is the need to generate knowledge and to Pagina 6 de 7 build capacity, in addition to the urgent and necessary data mitigation. The BCB is highly attentive to the discussions on sustainable finance, especially the debate on taxonomy, a fundamental aspect for the evolution of the sustainability agenda on several fronts. The lack of standardization in the classification system of sustainable or green assets, that is, the taxonomy, is one of the main challenges for the deepening and maturing of the sustainable finance market. Defining the taxonomy for financial assets is essential to have a common language and a standard, which will subsequently bring about a better understanding of the impact of the investments being done, as well as reduce asymmetries and conflicting views on the same practices. Furthermore, the resulting taxonomy and standardization could generate a virtuous circle that can accelerate changes in the financial system and galvanize the financing towards more sustainable practices or needed increase in cleaner energy, for example. This is a field that needs further advancement, and we are maintaining a close dialogue with many players of the financial system. Cooperation is much appreciated here. Thank you! Pagina 7 de 7

Title: Speech by Director Fernanda Guardado at a meeting with investors of UBS Brasil Administradora de Valores.
text: CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL Brasilia, November 10, 2022 Director Fernanda Guardado - UBS Event Good morning, Alexandre, and to all those who are with us this morning. It is a pleasure to be with you here today, and I would like to thank UBS for the invitation. I will dedicate my speech today to the topic of uncertainty. A quote on the topic that I really like states: "Uncertainty is worse than knowing the truth, no matter how bad". In fact, above-usual uncertainty has been one of the hallmarks of economic cycles since the beginning of the pandemic. Related to several sources, the high uncertainty that has surrounded the economic outlook has changed its face and impacted not only economic policy decisions but also their results, with implications for how to act and react in the coming periods. As we approach the end of 2022, however, some uncertainties resolve themselves while other uncertainties remain. The Ukraine War, for example, points to a long duration with lasting impacts on the energy supply and possibly grains in the region. The inflationary process that began to take shape at the end of 2020 proved more persistent than expected, leading to the highest inflation rates in more than 40 years in several advanced economies. The world has learned to live with the virus. We also noticed that part of the displacements in supply and production chains derived from the pandemic have been decreasing, even though there are problems related to the fight against Covid in China. The normalization of production chains and the reduction of the imbalance between supply and demand in the goods sector translate into lower pressures on goods inflation, which was one of the first drivers of the global inflationary process. Combined with the costs related to the necessary energy transition and the below-necessary investments in energy generation in recent years, commodity prices have advanced sharply, impacting food and energy inflation globally, but have been showing accommodation recently. volatile segments, such as commodities and goods, for services inflation. In fact, in several countries there is an acceleration of inflation in services to high levels in a heated labor market environment. This process is usually characterized by greater inertia, and requires monetary authorities to take more forceful action, in order to ensure the return of inflation to levels compatible with its target and the anchoring of inflation expectations. Thus, greater clarity regarding the environment for global monetary policy is outlined: we have moved from the "low for long" environment to the "higher for longer" environment, characterized by interest rates at a contractionary level - and well above what was observed in the pre-pandemic period - for a few quarters ahead in both advanced and emerging countries. It should be noted, however, that in this cycle, emerging countries have taken the lead in the process of normalizing their monetary policies, and in particular the Central Bank of Brazil, which began its adjustment process in March 2021. In Brazil, this change in inflationary vectors has also been happening. In fact, it is observed that services inflation accelerated to 8.5% year-on-year in September's reading, the highest pace since 2015, while core industrial goods begins to give way in the same comparison, but still advances 11.5%. Inflation expectations, even for longer terms, have risen, reacting to inflationary surprises and risks surrounding the outlook. In his participation in the Jackson Hole Symposium in 2003, economist Cari Walsh brought an important lesson: the dangers of underestimating the degree of persistence of inflation seem to be greater than those associated with overestimating this persistence. Going back to the sentence at the beginning, when you don't know "how the persistence of the inflationary process will be, you should act as if it were very persistent. In this sense, it will be necessary to have serenity to observe how the disinflation process and the risks associated with this process will unfold in Brazil. Geopolitical uncertainties remain and those linked to structural developments, such as the reorganization of global production chains, with processes such as nearshoring and friendshoring, and the climate transition. Both may present opportunities for Brazil, but they also bring the prospect of price pressures associated with changing suppliers and locations, and a more pressured energy supply in an environment where severe weather events have become more frequent. There is now some debate about the level of the output gap in the Brazilian economy, which may be closer to neutrality. In this case, the impacts on inflation tend to be more persistent, if the gap is smaller than estimated. Measuring the output gap in a contemporary way is always difficult, but even more so in a scenario like the current one, surrounded by enormous uncertainties even about possible structural changes. But we are confident that, as a reflection of the monetary tightening undertaken since March 2021, the direction of the gap in the coming quarters is towards greater openness. The Central Bank will remain attentive to uncertainties and prospective developments, acting independently, persevering in its strategy until it has confidence in the process of convergence of inflation and expectations for the target. The Central Bank will remain vigilant and serene, following the uncertainties and how the disinflation process evolves. Thanks.
