Vou dedicar minha fala hoje ao tema da incerteza. Uma citao sobre o tema que gosto bastante afirma: Uncertainty is worse than knowing the truth, no matter how bad. De fato, a incerteza acima do usual tem sido umas das caractersticas marcantes dos ciclos econmicos desde o incio da pandemia. Relacionado a diversas fontes, a incerteza elevada que tem cercado as perspectivas econmicas tem mudado de face e impactado no apenas as decises de poltica econmica como seus resultados, com implicaes sobre como agir e reagir nos prximos perodos.  medida que nos aproximamos do fim de 2022, entretanto, algumas incertezas se resolvem enquanto outras incertezas permanecem. A Guerra da Ucrnia, por exemplo, aponta para uma durao longa e com impactos duradouros sobre a oferta energtica e possivelmente de gros na regio. O processo inflacionrio que comeou a se delinear em fins de 2020 se provou mais persistente que o esperado, ensejando as maiores taxas de inflao em mais de 40 anos em diversas economias avanadas. O mundo aprendeu a conviver com o vrus. Percebemos tambm que parte dos deslocamentos de oferta e de cadeias produtivas derivados da pandemia vm diminuindo, ainda que se observem problemas relacionados ao combate ao Covid na China. As normalizaes das cadeias produtivas e a diminuio do desequilbrio entre oferta e demanda no setor de bens se traduzem em menores presses na inflao de bens, que foi um dos primeiros propulsores do processo inflacionrio global. Aliado aos custos relacionados  necessria transio energtica e aos investimentos abaixo do necessrio em gerao de energia dos ltimos anos, os preos de commodities avanaram acentuadamente, impactando a inflao de alimentos e energia globalmente, mas tm apontado acomodao recentemente. Pgina 2 de 4 segmentos volteis, como commodities e bens, para a inflao de servios. De fato, em vrios pases observa-se uma acelerao da inflao de servios para patamares altos em ambiente de mercado de trabalho aquecido. Este processo costuma ser caracterizado por uma maior inrcia, e exige das autoridades monetrias uma ao mais contundente, de modo a garantir o retorno da inflao para patamares compatveis com sua meta e a ancoragem das expectativas de inflao. Assim, uma maior clareza em relao ao ambiente para a poltica monetria global se delineia: samos do ambiente de low for long para o ambiente de higher for longer, caracterizado por taxas de juros em patamar contracionista - e bem acima do observado no pr-pandemia - por alguns trimestres  frente tanto nos pases avanados quanto nos emergentes. Nota- se, entretanto, que neste ciclo, os pases emergentes saram na frente no processo de normalizao de suas polticas monetrias, e em particular o Banco Central do Brasil, que iniciou seu processo de ajuste em maro de 2021. No Brasil, essa mudana de vetores inflacionrios tambm vem acontecendo. De fato, observa-se que a inflao de servios acelerou para 8,5% em termos interanuais na leitura de setembro, o maior ritmo desde 2015, enquanto o ncleo de bens industriais comea a ceder na mesma comparao, mas ainda avana 11,5%. As expectativas de inflao, mesmo para prazos mais longos, subiram, reagindo a surpresas inflacionrias e aos riscos em torno do cenrio prospectivo. Em sua participao no Simpsio de Jackson Hole em 2003, o economista Cari Walsh trouxe uma lio importante: os perigos de se subestimar o grau de persistncia da inflao parecem ser maiores que os associados  superestimao desta persistncia. Voltando  frase do incio, ao no saber how bacT ser a persistncia do processo inflacionrio, deve-se agir como se muito persistente fosse. Neste sentido, ser necessrio ter serenidade para observar como o processo de desinflao e os riscos associados a este processo se desenrolaro no Brasil. Pgina 3 de 4 Permanecem as incertezas geopolticas e ligadas desenvolvimentos estruturais, como a reorganizao das cadeias de produo globais, com processos como nearshoring e friendshoring, e  transio climtica. Ambos podem apresentar oportunidades para o Brasil, mas trazem tambm a perspectivas de presses de preos associadas  mudana de fornecedores e localizaes, e de uma oferta de energia mais pressionada em ambiente onde os eventos climticos graves tem se tornado mais frequentes. H hoje algum debate sobre o nvel do hiato do produto da economia brasileira, que pode estar mais prximo da neutralidade. Neste caso, os impactos sobre a inflao tendem a ser mais persistentes, caso o hiato seja menor que o estimado. Medir o hiato do produto de forma contempornea  sempre difcil, mas mais ainda em um cenrio como o atual, cercado por enormes incertezas inclusive sobre possveis mudanas estruturais. Mas estamos confiantes que, como reflexo do aperto monetrio empreendido desde maro de 2021, a direo do hiato nos prximos trimestres  no sentido de uma maior abertura. O Banco Central seguir atento s incertezas e aos desenvolvimentos prospectivos, agindo de maneira independente, perseverando em sua estratgia at que tenha confiana no processo de convergncia da inflao e das expectativas para a meta. O BC seguir vigilante e sereno, acompanhando as incertezas e como evolui o processo de desinflao. Obrigada. Pgina 4 de 4

Title: Speech by the Director of International Affairs and Corporate Risk Management, Fernanda Guardado, at the opening of the High-Level Seminar on Central Banking: Past and Present Challenges, promoted by the Central Bank. - 68.6 Kb
text: HL Seminar on Central Banking Good afternoon Roberto, Minister Fernando Haddad, Governors, fellow Deputy Governors, invited speakers, and guests. Welcome to the first High Level Seminar of the Central Bank of Brazil. The aim of our gathering today is to share insights, experiences and lessons on monetary policy and central banking in general, from present and former policymakers. Cooperation and the constant sharing of insights is one of the many qualities of the Central Bank community, and with today's seminar, the BCB also aims to share some of these discussions and insights with a broader audience. Talking of cooperation and sharing, I would like to highlight how the staff at the BCB and its International Affairs Department - Derin, in particular, work hard at keeping and improving international relationships with other Central Banks and international institutions. Just to give some quick numbers, the BCB had over 900 interactions with foreign counterparts in 2022 alone - embracing the relationship with other central banks, supervisory authorities, international organizations and forums, international portfolio investors, global rating agencies, cooperation or development agencies, government bodies, regional blocks of countries, among others. The BCB actively contributed to almost 60 international working groups during the year, in different areas. These interactions aim to discuss and incorporate best practices and policies, recommendations from standard setting bodies, exchanges on economic developments domestically and abroad, and also learn as much as possible from the experiences of others in order to better serve our society. All of this would notbepossiblewithouttheBCBs highly committed staff. The result of these efforts is visible not only in the great line up of todays seminar, but also in several endeavors with other CBs, monetary authorities and international organizations. The BCB is highly regarded by its peers on the many activities it pursues, ranging from monetary policy to financial regulation, supervision practices and the newer digital payments and green agendas. In fact, the BCB is a member of the Board of the BIS, the IMFC at the IMF, the Steering Committee of the NGFS, the board of the FSB, the Junta of the Cemla, as well as a recurring participant in all major economic global forums. In 2024, the BCB and the Ministry of Finance will be jointly organizing and hosting the Finance Track of the G20 in Brazil, a project which we are very excited about and proud of being a part of. Back to todays seminar, we look forward to discussions ranging from structural challenges that have surrounded central banking to the most current challenges, related to an environment of persistently high inflation. Indeed, the past quarters have been characterized by a synchronized tightening cycle in the face of the largest inflationary spell since the 1970s, and more recently, banking stresses have further complicated the environment. But, luckly, much has been learned in the previous decades to help us address this scenario: the importance of CB autonomy, Inflation targeting, strong regulatory frameworks, the separation principle and so on. Among the lessons learned are also the benefits of acting fast and being committed to low inflation, and that credibility and anchored inflation expectations are key for successful disinflations and a more predictable economy. I am sure that each panelist will add different perspectives and backgrounds to this debate, and I very much look forward to hearing your insights. With that, I am very pleased to give the floor now to Minister Fernando Haddad, who will give the opening remarks of our seminar.

Title: COP 26 - A Financial System for the Net Zero
text: A Financial System for the Net Zero DATE: Wednesday, November 3, 2021 TIME: 10:15-11:30 Session 2 - "Climate Risk is Financial Risk" Question: The BCB has been leading in managing physical and transition risks launching your comprehensive Sustainability Agenda in September 2020. What are the lessons you have learnt from this work and how important this is for a country exposed to both the physical and transition risks from climate change?  The greatest lesson for all of us is that sustainability issues have become increasingly important for society. o Climate and environmental issues, which have long been major topics on the international agenda, have gained even more importance afterthe pandemic.  Within climate risks, both physical and transition risks represent significant challenges going forward.  The financial system is closely linked to those risks, not only to the adverse impacts they may bring on their portfolios, but also to the effects that financial institutions generate on the environment. o For instance, in terms of emissions from reporting financial institutions in Brazil, from 2011 to 2014, they grew around 51%. Since then, they have been reducing, returning in 2020 to the same levels of 2011 (675 thousands of tons of CO2  In addition, climate issues involve not only risks but also opportunities for the financial system. And we have seen progress in this area recently. o Just to give an example, issuance of green and sustainability-linked bonds in Brazil has grown from US 600 million in 2015 to almost US 8 billion in 2021 year-to- date, according to Reuters.  To deal with these challenges and opportunities, central banks need to remain on the frontier of knowledge and actions, responding: o to the evolution of society's demands; o to structural changes in the economy; and o to current and future shocks and risks.  For central banks, having a sustainability agenda is important because sustainability issues have the potential to affect their two main mandates: o Monetary policy and financial stability. BCB's Sustainability Agenda  Of course, these issues are important for a country rich in natural resources like Brazil. o And we have taken the opportunity to advance further in the sustainability agenda.  Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) has a long history of supporting the environmental agenda, implementing measures related to the subject and actively participating in the international debate. o Especially in the last decade, the BCB issued several regulations with the aim of starting the integration of social and environmental factors in the risk analysis of financial institutions. In 2014, the BCB established the guidelines of socio-environmental responsibility policies for Brazilian the financial institutions; In 2017, we included social and environmental risk among those that financial institutions must identify, measure, assess, control and mitigate.  As you mentioned in your question, in September 2020 the BCB launched a broader sustainability agenda as an additional pillar of its strategic agenda for the development of the financial system (Agenda BC#).  With our Sustainability Agenda we aim to lead by example within the Brazilian financial system and to deliver concrete results to society, in line with the best international practices. In terms of greenhouse gas emissions from reporting institutions of the Brazilian Financial System, they amounted to 675 thousandsoftonsof CO 2 equivalent in 2011, then grew to 1020 thousands of tons of CO2 equivalent in 2014. Later they moderated to 918 thousands of tons of CO2 equivalent in 2019, and back to 675 thousands of tons of CO2 equivalent in 2020 with the Covid-19 pandemic. The Brazilian Public Registry includes emission data from thefinancial institutions themselves, and some of their upstream and downstream supply chain, but not yet from the counterparts of their loan operations. Pagina2de4  Since the topic of this panel is on risk management, I will focus on the supervisory and regulatory actions of our agenda related to risk management.  On the supervisory front, the BCB is developingthe following actions: o Structuring and expanding the collection of information on social and environmental risks. o Stress tests for climate risks. Inclusion of climate risk scenarios in new and improved stress tests performed by the BCB, in line with international best practices.  Regarding regulation, the BCB has sought to dialogue with society. o For this, the BCB has made use of public consultations to receive contributions from various segments of society.  In 2021, for example, two important issues were regulated after being the object of a public consultation: o The ESG Risk Management and Policy and o The Disclosure of ESG Policy. o The former extends regulatory requirements applicable to the management of traditional risks to social, environmental and climate-related risks, on an integrated risk managementframework. Furthermore, the Social, Environmental and Climate Responsibility Policy (PRSAC) improves the requirement that financial institutions develop and disclose a Socio-Environmental Responsibility Policy, including climate- related responsibility. o The latter improves the requirements for implementing a transparent and standardized reporting of the Social, Environmental and Climate risks and opportunities of financial institutions. In Brazil, the scope of this initiative goes beyondthe climate perspective of TCFD and has been expandedtoinclude social and environmental issues. o We understand that the development of a sustainability agenda requires some time, and therefore requires a gradual timeline for a feasible implementation. For example, in the disclosure of ESG risks, the BCB will request from financial institutions first qualitative information, and at a later stage quantitative information.  Also on the regulatory front, one of BCB's most important actions in progress is the implementation of a Sustainable Rural Credit Bureau (Green Bureau). ESG Risk Management(ResolutionsCMN4943,4944/2021); ESG Policy(ResolutionCMN4945/2021); Social, Environmental and Climate Disclosure (Resolution BCB 139/2021) Pagina3de4 concessions, which will make it possible to characterize rural credit operations with social, environmental and climate additionalities. o The Green Bureau will be a tool for risk management by financial institutions, improving asset pricing and access to new sources of resources, under an Open Finance framework.  I would like to point out that the objective of this agenda is, within the BCB's mandate, to induce the conditions for the developmentofsustainable finances in the national financial system, which includes: o The best international practices related to sustainable finance; o Greater availability of resources for sustainable enterprises; and o Better management of social, environmental and climate risks. Conclusion  Looking ahead, climate transition is likely to pose increasing costs and challenges for the economy and the society. o In order to face this transition in a more appropriate way, the BCB will support the development of proper financial market instruments, since these instruments are able to promote a more efficient resource allocation.  Our Sustainability Agenda is extensive, but by no means exhaustive.  Ultimately, the BCB will seek to continue on the frontier of the knowledge and actions linked to social, environmental and climate issues. o The institution will act, within its mandate, to address present and future challenges related to these topics, as these are fields in constant evolution. Resolution BCB 140/2021 already prohibits ere ditto agents with illegal social, environmental and climate practices. The Green Bureau is scheduled to be implemented until June 2022. Pagina4de4

Title: COP 26 - The Central Banks and Supervisors Network for Geening the Financial System
text: "The Central Banks and Supervisors Network for Greening the Financial System: achievements and ways forward" DATE: Wednesday, November 3, 2021 TIME: 14:30-15:05 Session 2 - "Climate Risk is Financial Risk" Question: How has the NGFS been useful to central banks and supervisors, but also to the financial community as a whole? Good afternoon, Jean. Good afternoon to all. It is always a pleasure to talk about sustainability issues, and in particular on the importance of the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) to central banks, supervisors, and, as a consequence, to the entire financial community. I am also proud to say that I am a member of the Board of a Central Bank that became member of the NGFS in 2020, and that brings sustainability as one of its strategic objectives. Let me start by saying that tackling climate risks and the massive challenges that come with them demands a global answer. Values such as information sharing, coordination, and the promotion of a better understanding on climate related issues are highly welcome, and it is precisely at these points that the NGFS has demonstrated one of its greatest merits. Since its launch in 2017, with only a few central banks kicking off a much-needed debate, it has grown to currently 95 and 16 observers willing, on a voluntary basis, to share best practices and to contribute to the analysis and management of climate and environment-related risks in the financial sector, as well as to mobilize mainstream finance to support the transition toward a sustainable economy. In other words, we can say that it is difficult to talk nowadays about the role of central banks on the sustainability front without thinking about the NGFS. After the publication of the April 2019 NGFS Comprehensive Report, members collectively acknowledged that climate-related risks are a source of financial risk and that more work on practical deliverables were needed. Among the report's highly welcome recommendations, four were especially aimed at inspiring central banks and supervisors to take best practices on board:  Integrating climate-related risks into financial stability monitoring and micro-supervision.  Integrating sustainability factors into own portfolio management.  Bridging the data gaps.  Building awareness and intellectual capacity. I can say that, despite already having a long tradition of supporting ESG initiatives and the environmental and climate-related agenda, these NGFS recommendations were great inspirations for the BCB's Sustainability Strategic Dimension, in September 2020. Since its Comprehensive Report, the NGFS has focused on the follow-up of these recommendations and its resulting Guides have played an important role in this endeavor. The reports on climate scenarios are especially important for central banks, such as the BCB, who are developing their stress tests on climate risks, and the scenarios developed by the NGFS, on one hand, will help to develop comparable exercises across jurisdictions, but also allow sufficient flexibility for the scenarios to be adapted to each country specificity or relevant exercise. I would now like to focus on one of the most recent contributions of the Network, in which the Banco Central do Brasil actively helped to build: The Progress Report on the Guide for Supervisors. Pagina 2 de 3 This report brings practical guidance and case studies identified among NGFS members, showing great progress in the integration of climate and environmental risks into supervisory frameworks. Some recommendations have evolved quite positively:  Development of a clear strategy, establishment of an internal organization and allocation of adequate resources to address climate-related and environmental risks; and  Setting of supervisory expectations to create transparency for financial institutions in relation to the supervisors' understanding of a prudent approach to climate-related and environmental risks. This report identifies focus areas to better assist supervisors. Depending on progress made so far and specific needs, a supervisor can choose to dwell into selected focus areas, learning from the experience of others and deciding whether to adopt or adapt the good practices accordingly. The Progress Report also provides a deeper dive into a few identified areas, especially environmental risks and disclosure - both of them representing a less developed field in which the NGFS can help its members to understand better and deliver more concrete actions. This agenda is evolving swiftly, but further work is still necessary, especially in relation to data gaps, lack of harmonized methodologies and risk metrics, and insufficient internal capacity and resources. Through its current and upcoming NGFS initiatives, the Network can elevate not only supervisory capabilities and convergence of global supervisory practices, but the whole sustainability agenda, helping central banks and supervisory agencies to foster better and more tailored approaches for environmental and climate-related issues. And as central banks and supervisory agencies are beacons for national financial systems, a virtuous cycle will proceed. Thank you very much. Pagina 3 de 3

Title: Notes by the Director of Relationship, Citizenship and Conduct Supervision, Maurcio Moura, at the IV Forum of Public Management Faciap, in Curitiba (PR). - 197 Kb
text: The CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL Brasilia, March 29, 2022. Notes from the Director of Relationship, Citizenship and Conduct Supervision of the Central Bank, Mauricio Moura Event: IV Public Management Forum - FACIAP - Economic Scenario and BC Agenda# Panel: The Importance of the Financial System in the Real Economy Good afternoon everyone! I greet those who are present with us and, in particular, those who participate in the opening of this panel:  Manfred Dasenbrock - President of Central Sicredi PR/SP/RJ  Wilson Geraldo Cavina - Chairman of the Board of Directors of Sicoob Central Unicoob  Alzimiro Thome - Chief Executive Officer of Central Cresol Baser  Hilgo Goncalves - Vice-President of the Federation of Commercial and Business Associations of Parana (FACIAP)  Colleagues from the Central Bank, Paulo Sergio and Otavio Damaso It is a pleasure to participate in this panel of the IV Edition of the Public Management Forum of the Federation of Commercial and Business Associations of Parana (FACIAP). In the position of regulator and supervisor of the financial system, the Central Bank's concern with the customers and users of the system involves the need for the offer of products and services to be adequate to each individual and market agent and to promote their conscious use. All of us citizens want the benefits of a sound and efficient financial system, with better financial services that are tailored to our needs, with the participation of all. This is what we call Financial Democratization at the Central Bank. In this context, the theme of financial education and its importance for the citizen, for the development of a sustainable National Financial System and for sustainable economic growth gains new contours and takes on a central character. For the Central Bank, the topic is so relevant that the Education dimension is one of the five pillars of the BC# Agenda. The Education dimension aims to raise awareness among citizens so that everyone participates in the market and cultivates the habit of saving. In this sense, the participation of market agents, such as cooperatives, class associations, microcredit distributors, and government agents, is key. Financial education has the potential to change people's behavior, making them capable of making conscious and autonomous choices that meet their needs and life goals. In a broader sense, the Education dimension is contained in the Central Bank's effort to promote the inclusion and financial health of citizens, giving millions of people the opportunity to make dreams come true and improve their lives through the proper management of their finances. Financial inclusion and financial health are intrinsically related. Financial inclusion is linked to the framework necessary for all market participants to develop their full economic potential. It should be seen as an action for the long-term sustainability of the financial system and the economy of a country itself. Financial inclusion has the potential to catalyze a country's economic development and bring positive social impacts, especially for disadvantaged populations. Following the current scenario of rapid technological evolution, products and services can be complex for a relevant layer of the population. Therefore, inclusion needs to take place in an appropriate way so that each citizen can not only find appropriate solutions for themselves in the Financial System, but also be prepared to use them to their advantage. This demands user focus, simplicity, and convenience. In this context, I could not fail to mention Pix as a great driver of adequate financial inclusion. Pix decisively impacts this process by reducing consumer costs, especially for individuals, individual microentrepreneurs (MEIs) and individual entrepreneurs, in addition to opening possibilities for service providers and bringing gains to the real economy. Financial health, in turn, can be translated as financial well-being. To be financially healthy is to be able to consume responsibly and consciously, to have knowledge that allows you to make appropriate choices of financial products and services linked to your needs. The vector that helps in the process of greater financial inclusion and in improving the financial health of the population is financial education. However, the Central Bank alone does not have the capacity to bring financial education to the entire Brazilian population, considering the continental dimensions of our country and its cultural diversity. It is through permanent action at the national level and the formation of partnerships between public agencies and private institutions that we will be able to reach the entire Brazilian population. No one is granted a monopoly or market reserve in any area related to financial education. The more people and organizations engage in this journey, the deeper and more comprehensive the benefits will be for the entire Brazilian society. Among the actions that have been developed by the Central Bank in the area of financial education, I would like to highlight the Learning Value Program. Aprender Valor is the Financial Education Program in public elementary schools. Bringing Financial Education to public schools across the country would not be possible without the partnership with the Center for Public Policies and Education Evaluation, of the Federal University of Juiz de Fora (CAEd/UFJF) and without the financial support of the Fund for the Defense of Diffuse Rights of the Ministry of Justice and Public Security (FDD/MJSP). The Learning Value Program seeks to support secretariats, public elementary schools and teachers in the implementation of the teaching of Financial Education in the classroom as a cross-cutting theme, as prescribed by the National Common Curriculum Base (BNCC). I highlight some numbers that represent the magnitude achieved by Aprender Valor so far:  More than 15 thousand schools joined the Program in the 27 Federation Units and in 2,200 municipalities - representing more than a third of Brazilian municipalities - covering a universe of 88 thousand education professionals and almost 932 thousand students from IO to 9th grade.  Almost 300 thousand evaluations of 5th, 7th and 9th grade students were carried out under the Program. More than 35 thousand classes were taught, using school projects in which Financial Education is integrated with Mathematics, Portuguese Language and Human Sciences.  Almost 8 thousand education professionals have completed training for managers and teachers, including training in Personal Financial Education.  More specifically, the numbers in Parana stand out, with 70 thousand students registered in 1,300 participating schools. This represents % of Parana's schools, covering almost 70% of the state's municipalities. I take this opportunity to remind all managers of fundamental public education in the country that on March 31 the phase of adhesion to the Program for this year 2022 ends. Don't miss the chance to positively impact the lives of our children and young people! Contact and join your school! I cannot fail to mention, also, within the scope of financial education actions, the partnership with the cooperative sector. The Central Bank has in the National Cooperative Credit System (SNCC) a great ally for the promotion of financial education. In the last ENEF Week, for example, cooperatives reached more than 23 million people through lectures, courses or digital initiatives. But the commitment of credit unions in Financial Education goes beyond the events held on special dates. Financial Education is in the DNA of cooperatives, in their 5th and 7th Cooperative Principles: education, training and information and interest in the community. The credit cooperative sector carries out, with excellence, the dissemination of Financial Education from its own educational programs, courses and lectures. In the last mapping carried out by the Central Bank, in 2021, with the participation of 619 cooperatives linked to 2nd and 3rd level systems, we identified more than 2,000 Financial Education actions. But we have room for improvement! The Central Bank has been acting at a strategic level with institutes, foundations, confederations and other members of the National Cooperative Credit System. We want to seek the improvement of Financial Education programs, particularly in monitoring and evaluation activities, thus expanding their reach and creating even more value for the cooperative members and, consequently, for the communities where they are inserted. We seek to build with cooperatives a transformation in their organizational culture. We want Financial Education integrated into the cooperatives' business, permeating all their work processes. In the monitoring carried out by the Central Bank, we can already identify some fruits of this transformation. We identify cooperatives managing their performance through indicators that include the performance of Financial Education activities and the satisfaction of their members; and cooperative systems developing new products and applications for mobile banking with the participation of teams specialized in Financial Education. It is important to emphasize that at the current stage of development of financial education actions, there is a need for broad dialogue and exchange of experience among credit unions. Many initiatives are under development and we need the sector, as a whole, to be able to walk together and in an articulated way. The Central Bank encourages inter-cooperative dialogues. Finally, we want to emphasize the confidence that the Central Bank has in the ability of cooperatives to achieve excellence in the mission of Financial Education, generating gains not only for their members, but also for the communities where they are present. I believe that with the initiatives mentioned and many others under development, related to the education dimension, we are taking concrete steps to ensure the sustainable development of our country's economy, to the extent that these initiatives bring benefits to all involved. I thank you for the opportunity and wish you all an excellent event.

Title: Notes by Director Maurcio Moura at the Seminar "The treatment of the over-indebted consumer in the light of Law No. 14,181/2021: from the legislative trajectory to its effectiveness", promoted by the STJ and CNJ.
text: The CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL Brasilia, November 30, 2022. Notes from the Director of Relationship, Citizenship and Conduct Supervision of the Central Bank, Mauricio Moura Event: The Treatment of the Over-indebted Consumer of Law No. 14,181/2021 Over-indebtedness under the economic perspective Good morning.  I thank you for the invitation to participate in this panel.  I would like to begin by greeting all the magistrates, prosecutors, public defenders, civil servants, mediators, lawyers, journalists and students present here.  In particular, I want to greet my fellow panelists: Isaac Sidney, President of Febraban; Eric Universo Rodrigues Brasil, Partner and Executive Director of Tendencias Consultoria Integrada; and our moderator, Vicente de Chiara, Legal Director of Febraban.  The Central Bank's concern with the phenomenon of over-indebtedness from an economic perspective unfolds into two main and interdependent strands.  The first, at the individual level: it is the concern for the citizen and their families.  Over-indebtedness brings economic and emotional losses not only to individuals, but also to their families, especially and more severely, among the lower-income population.  The recent release of the results of the World Bank's Global Findex survey points out that almost half of the people with the lowest income cannot live on what they earn and, consequently, have difficulty creating savings or setting medium and long-term goals.  The second strand is related to the systemic aspect of over-indebtedness.  Considering the BC's legal mandate to ensure a stable and efficient financial system, we know that growing levels of indebtedness can, at the limit, put this stability at risk, with serious consequences for the economy and the population.  The importance that the Central Bank gives to the issue of over-indebtedness is reflected in our strategic agenda, the BC# Agenda, a work agenda  Therefore, the Central Bank has been monitoring and supporting actions for its prevention and treatment.  On the prevention side, the Central Bank and the National Monetary Council impose rules for granting responsible credit to the financial system.  This is already an old commitment of the Central Bank, dating back to 2006 and 2007, when the first rules were published to ensure, respectively, free credit portability and transparency of the Total Effective Cost.  In 2009, this commitment was expanded with the publication of CMN Resolution No. 3,694, which included the implementation of internal controls by financial institutions, in order to ensure the transparency of information for decision-making by customers and the adequacy of the products and services offered or recommended to the needs, interests and objectives of their users.  Law No. 14,181, of 2021, by amending the Consumer Protection Code, brought important advances to ensure that the granting of credit is even more responsible, both by members of the National Financial System and by other sectors of the economy, ensuring the preservation of the existential minimum and the regulation of the advertising offer, among other aspects.  Based on these changes, the Central Bank engaged in updating the Guide of Excellence in the Offer of Financial Products and Services - Credit Operations, a product whose main objective is to disclose practices to be adopted by financial institutions to promote responsible credit and for consumer financial education.  Due to the representativeness of this event at the CNJ, I am happy to inform you that we take this opportunity to launch today the result of this work: the 3rd edition of the Guide of Excellence.  As in previous editions, the Guide provides examples of procedures for the practice of responsible credit, in addition to indicating the need for broad collaboration between institutions and the bodies responsible for conciliation in the pre-judicial phase of the treatment of over-indebtedness, in order to make this flow more agile and less costly for all involved.  We hope that this new version will be even more useful for the National Financial System, for the National Consumer Protection System and for the Judiciary.  Returning to the Central Bank, Education is one of the five pillars of our BC# Agenda, which includes financial education actions to prevent over-indebtedness.  The Central Bank's strategy in financial education is based on the PLA-POU-CRe tripod, an acronym for planning, active savings, and conscious credit, elements that must go together.  Only with the planning of the personal and family budget is it possible to control the accounts to save actively, without waiting for any surplus of money at the end of the month, but "paying yourself first".  With planning, it is also possible to take credit only when necessary, consciously, knowing how much you can pay per month and opting for the most appropriate alternative for the borrower's needs.  The PLA-POU-CRe tripod is the basis of our financial education program with elementary schools, the Learning Value Program, which, sponsored by the Fund for the Defense of Diffuse Rights of the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, has already reached 17 thousand schools and reached 1.3 million students in more than 40% of the municipalities in Brazil. in all Brazilian states.  But this tripod is also the basis of our targeting of financial and payment institutions in their performance in financial education.  BCB Communique No. 34,201, of 2019, expressly states that institutions must act in accordance with the guidelines of the PLA-POU-CRe and we have seen a growing number of financial institutions acting on the subject.  In our last mapping with banks, financial institutions and payment institutions, of the 53 institutions consulted, 51 had some type of financial education action.  But we want to go further: our goal is for financial education to take even deeper roots in the governance of these institutions, permeating their processes so that they can even better fulfill their role of providing products and services appropriate to the needs, interests, and objectives of their customers.  I want to highlight the importance of the credit cooperative sector, which has financial education in its DNA, as it is present in the cooperative principles.  The cooperative sector works on financial education in conjunction with the provision of financial services.  The Central Bank has supported this articulation, encouraging all cooperatives to participate in this movement.  In the last mapping of financial education actions, carried out by the Central Bank in 2021, of the 630 cooperatives consulted, 84% worked in some way with financial education.  Our goal is to engage 100%!  The Central Bank has also acted together with class associations.  With Febraban, I highlight the development of the Meu Bolso em Dia platform, which has tools and knowledge trails specially developed for consumers who are in debt and can help them organize their finances and negotiate more effectively with institutions a solution to their credit situation.  I also consider it important to highlight the new edition of the Financial Negotiation and Guidance Task Force, launched in November by Febraban and the Central Bank, in partnership with Senacon, and which this month warned about over-indebtedness, how to identify it and where to seek specialized help.  As for the treatment of over-indebtedness, the Central Bank is renewing the technical cooperation agreement with Senacon, which will allow even greater interaction between the two bodies.  This partnership will be useful to diffuse the flows for the global renegotiations, once they are defined.  I also highlight that the Central Bank monitors what we call "risky indebtedness" - composed only of debts with the SFN, therefore, much more restricted than over-indebtedness.  By "risky indebtedness" we mean the situation in which borrowers have at least two of the following characteristics: o Default of more than 90 days; o Monthly disposable income, after debt service payment, below the poverty line; o Simultaneous exposure to more onerous credit modalities; and Commitment of more than 50% of monthly income to debt service payment.  In Brazil, according to the latest survey, with data from June 2022, there are 12.2 million people in a situation of risky indebtedness, or 12.2% of borrowers in authorized financial institutions.  It is important to be clear that this does not mean that there are 12.2 million over-indebted people in Brazil, because the concepts are different, since the characterization of over-indebtedness depends on specific and qualitative data of each citizen, to which the Central Bank does not have access.  The monitoring of risky indebtedness by the Central Bank is important so that we can direct information to these people to provide them with the capacity to act when necessary, including initiating over-indebtedness treatment processes such as those established by Law 14,181, of 2021.  Finally, the Central Bank has been monitoring the first cases of treatment of over-indebtedness in accordance with Law 14,181, in order to ensure that the availability of credit - for customers outside the situation of over-indebtedness - is not impacted, especially for the lower-income population.  I understand that the purpose of Law 14,181 is to protect the consumer and reintegrate him into the consumption and credit system and not to create obstacles to his financial inclusion and access to credit.  The careful calibration of parameters brought by the Law is a fundamental measure to avoid negative externalities that may, in the medium term, put citizens and society in a worse situation than the current one.  I am sure that debates promoted in events such as the one taking place today shed light on a topic that needs to be faced with courage, determination and serenity and bring important inputs to continue advancing together on this agenda in favor of the financial health and well-being of the Brazilian population.  I thank you again for the invitation and wish you all an excellent event.

A preocupao do Banco Central com o fenmeno do superendividamento sob a perspectiva econmica se desdobra em duas vertentes principais e interdependentes.  A primeira, no nvel individual:  a preocupao com o cidado e com suas famlias.  O superendividamento traz prejuzos econmicos e emocionais no s para os indivduos, mas tambm para suas famlias, especialmente e com maior gravidade, entre a populao de menor renda.  A recente divulgao dos resultados da pesquisa Global Findex, do Banco Mundial, aponta que quase metade das pessoas de menor renda no consegue viver com o que ganha e, consequentemente, tem dificuldade em criar poupana ou estabelecer objetivos de mdio e longo prazos.  A segunda vertente est relacionada ao aspecto sistmico do superendividamento.  Considerando o mandato legal do BC de zelar por um sistema financeiro estvel e eficiente, sabemos que nveis crescentes de endividamento podem, no limite, colocar em risco essa estabilidade, com graves consequncias para a economia e para a populao.  A importncia que o Banco Central d a questo do superendividamento est refletida em nossa agenda estratgica, a Agenda BC#, uma pauta de trabalho Pgina 2 de 7  Por isso, o Banco Central vem acompanhando e apoiando aes para a sua preveno e o seu tratamento.  Do lado da preveno, o Banco Central e o Conselho Monetrio Nacional impem regras de concesso de crdito responsvel ao sistema financeiro.  Esse j  um compromisso antigo do BC, que remonta aos anos de 2006 e 2007, quando foram publicadas as primeiras normas para assegurar, respectivamente, a portabilidade gratuita de crdito e a transparncia do Custo Efetivo Total.  Em 2009, esse compromisso foi ampliado com a publicao da Resoluo CMN n 3.694, que contemplou a implementao de controles internos pelas instituies financeiras, de forma a assegurar a transparncia das informaes para tomada de deciso pelos clientes e a adequao dos produtos e servios ofertados ou recomendados s necessidades, interesses e objetivos de seus usurios.  A Lei n 14.181, de 2021, ao alterar o Cdigo de Defesa do Consumidor, trouxe importantes avanos para garantir que a concesso de crdito seja ainda mais responsvel, tanto pelos integrantes do Sistema Financeiro Nacional quanto por outros setores da economia, assegurando a preservao do mnimo existencial e a regulao da oferta publicitria, entre outros aspectos.  A partir dessas alteraes, o Banco Central se engajou na atualizao do Guia de Excelncia na Oferta de Produtos e Servios Financeiros - Operaes de Crdito, um produto cujo principal objetivo  divulgar prticas a serem adotadas pelas instituies financeiras para a promoo do crdito responsvel e para a educao financeira do consumidor.  Pela representatividade deste evento no CNJ, informo com alegria que aproveitamos essa oportunidade para lanar hoje o resultado desse trabalho: a 3a edio do Guia de Excelncia. Pgina 3 de 7  Como nas edies anteriores, o Guia traz exemplos de procedimentos para a prtica de crdito responsvel, alm de indicar a necessidade de ampla colaborao das instituies com os rgos responsveis pela conciliao na fase pr-judicial do tratamento do superendividamento, de forma a tornar esse fluxo mais gil e menos oneroso para todos os envolvidos.  Esperamos que essa nova verso seja ainda mais til para o Sistema Financeiro Nacional, para o Sistema Nacional de Defesa do Consumidor e para o Poder Judicirio.  Voltando ao Banco Central, Educao  um dos cinco pilares de nossa Agenda BC#, onde esto includas as aes de educao financeira para a preveno do superendividamento.  A estratgia do BC na educao financeira  baseada no trip PLA-POU-CR, um acrnimo para planejamento, poupana ativa e crdito consciente, elementos que devem caminhar juntos.  Apenas com o planejamento do oramento pessoal e familiar  possvel controlar as contas para poupar de forma ativa, sem esperar por eventual sobra de dinheiro no final do ms, e sim pagando-se primeiro.  Com planejamento tambm  possvel tomar crdito apenas quando necessrio, de forma consciente, sabendo quanto se pode pagar por ms e optando pela alternativa mais adequada para a necessidade do tomador.  O trip PLA-POU-CR  a base de nosso programa de educao financeira junto s escolas de ensino fundamental, o Programa Aprender Valor que, com patrocnio do Fundo de Defesa de Direitos Difusos do Ministrio da Justia e Segurana Pblica, j chegou a 17 mil escolas e alcanou 1,3 milho de alunos em mais de 40% dos municpios do Brasil, em todos os estados brasileiros.  Mas essetrip tambm  a base do nosso direcionamento para as instituies financeiras e de pagamentos em sua atuao em educao financeira.  O Comunicado BCB n 34.201, de 2019, traz expressamente que as instituies devem atuar nas diretrizes do PLA-POU-CR e temos visto um nmero crescente de instituies financeiras atuando no tema. Pgina4de7  Em nosso ltimo mapeamento com bancos, financeiras e instituies de pagamento, das 53 instituies consultadas, 51 possuam algum tipo de ao de educao financeira.  Mas queremos ir mais longe: nosso objetivo  que a educao financeira crie razes ainda mais profundas na governana dessas instituies, permeando seus processos para que elas possam cumprir ainda melhor seu papel de fornecer produtos e servios adequados s necessidades, interesses e objetivos de seus clientes.  Quero destacar a importncia do setor cooperativo de crdito, que tem a educao financeira em seu DNA, visto estar presente nos princpios cooperativistas.  O setor cooperativista trabalha educao financeira em conjunto com o oferecimento dos servios financeiros.  O Banco Central tem apoiado essa articulao, encorajando que todas as cooperativas participem desse movimento.  No ltimo mapeamento sobre aes de educao financeira, realizado pelo BC em 2021, das 630 cooperativas consultadas, 84% atuavam de alguma forma com educao financeira.  Nosso objetivo  engajar 100%!  O Banco Central tem atuado tambm em conjunto com as associaes de classe.  Com a Febraban, destaco o desenvolvimento da plataforma Meu Bolso em Dia, que possui ferramentas e trilhas de conhecimento especialmente desenvolvidas para consumidores que esto em situao de endividamento e que pode ajud-los a organizar suas finanas e negociar de maneira mais efetiva com as instituies uma soluo para sua situao creditcia.  Considero importante destacar, ainda, a nova edio do Mutiro de Negociao e Orientao Financeira, lanado em Io de novembro pela Febraban e pelo Banco Central, em parceria com a Senacon, e que neste ms alertou sobre o superendividamento, como identific-lo e onde buscar auxlio especializado. Pgina 5 de 7  Quanto ao tratamento ao superendividamento, o Banco Central est renovando o acordo de cooperao tcnica com a Senacon, o qual permitir ainda maior interao entre os dois rgos.  Essa parceria ser til para difundir os fluxos para as renegociaes globais, uma vez que estiverem definidos.  Destaco, ainda, que o Banco Central monitora o que denominamos endividamento de risco - composto apenas por dvidas junto ao SFN, portanto, bem mais restrito que o superendividamento.  Por endividamento de risco entenda-se a situao em que tomadores de crdito apresentam ao menos duas das seguintes caractersticas: o Inadimplncia superior a 90 dias; o Renda mensal disponvel, aps o pagamento do servio das dvidas, abaixo da linha da pobreza; o Exposio simultnea a modalidades de crdito mais onerosas; e o Comprometimento de mais de 50% da renda mensal com o pagamento do servio das dvidas.  No Brasil, segundo o ltimo levantamento, com dados de junho de 2022, h 12,2 milhes de pessoas em situao de endividamento de risco, ou 12,2% dos tomadores de crdito em instituies financeiras autorizadas.  Importante termos claro que isso no significa que h 12,2 milhes de superendividados no Brasil, pois os conceitos so diferentes, j que a caracterizao do superendividamento depende de dados especficos e qualitativos de cada cidado, aos quais o Banco Central no tem acesso.  O acompanhamento do endividamento de risco pelo Banco Central  importante para que possamos direcionar informao a essas pessoas para dot-las de capacidade para agir quando necessrio, inclusive iniciando processos de tratamento de superendividamento como os estabelecidos pela Lei 14.181, de 2021.  Finalmente, o Banco Central tem acompanhado os primeiros casos de tratamento de superendividamento nos moldes da Lei 14.181, de forma a Pgina6de7 assegurar que a disponibilidade de crdito - para clientes fora da situao de superendividamento - no seja impactada, principalmente para a populao de menor renda.  Entendo que o intuito da Lei 14.181  proteger o consumidor e reintegr-lo ao sistema de consumo e crdito e no criar obstculos para a sua incluso financeira e acesso a crdito.  A cuidadosa calibragem de parmetros trazidos pela Lei  medida fundamental para evitar externalidades negativas que possam, no mdio prazo, colocar o cidado e a sociedade em situao pior que a atual.  Estou certo de que debates promovidos em eventos como o que se realiza hoje lanam luz sobre um tema que precisa ser enfrentado com coragem, determinao e serenidade e trazem importantes insumos para seguirmos avanando juntos nessa agenda em prol da sade e bem-estar financeiros da populao brasileira.  Agradeo novamente o convite e desejo um excelente evento a todos. Pgina 7 de 7

Title: Notes by the Director of Relationship, Citizenship and Conduct Supervision, Maurcio Moura, at the event of the Learning Value Program  News of the 2023 cycle. - 131.2 Kb
text: The CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL Brasilia, May 30, 2023. Notes by the Director of Relationship, Citizenship and Conduct Supervision, Mauricio Moura, at the event of the Learning Value Program - News of the 2023 cycle  Good afternoon everyone! Welcome to this Learning Value event.  It is always a great satisfaction to meet with education professionals, partners who have embraced the proposal to bring financial education to our children and young people.  Today's event celebrates the joint advances we have made with Aprender Valor at the beginning of 2023 and reports on the program's news for this year.  I would like to emphasize the importance that Aprender Valor has for the Central Bank and, consequently, the relevance of the role played by you, our partners, in the implementation of the Program in your states and municipalities.  Learning Value was a dream cherished for years by the Central Bank and that became a reality thanks to the work of many hands.  Turning this dream into reality would not have been possible without our partnership with the Center for Public Policies and Education Evaluation, of the Federal University of Juiz de Fora (CAEd/UFJF) and without the financial contribution of the Fund for the Defense of Diffuse Rights of the Ministry of Justice and Public Security (FDD/MJSP).  Learning Value is one of the many initiatives of the Central Bank present in its strategic agenda, the BC# Agenda, a work agenda focused on technological evolution, which seeks to stimulate the offer of more adequate and higher quality financial services to the Brazilian population, in addition to the opportunity for everyone to participate in the market.  Aprender Valor helps students and education professionals in the search for improving their own and their families' financial well-being, by stimulating financial planning, active savings and the conscious use of credit, the already famous PLA-POU-CRe.  We are convinced that the Program has the potential to reach all 22 million elementary school students in public schools across the country, benefiting managers, teachers and students.  More than bringing financial education to the classrooms, we work so that this knowledge is taken by students to their respective families.  Children and young people are natural transmitters of knowledge and can become catalysts for the transformation of the use of money in their communities, improving the financial health of everyone around them, especially those families in situations of greater vulnerability.  This transformative power of financial education can lead to greater financial inclusion of the Brazilian population and has the ability to improve our socioeconomic indicators.  This motivates us to continue, attracting new participants and facing the challenges that always arise.  We have very expressive numbers for a program that has been running for only three years, two of which in the midst of the difficulties imposed by the Covid-19 pandemic.  Aprender Valor was launched for schools in 2020, in a pilot phase, in the same year that we suffered from the beginning of the Covid-19 pandemic.  As with the entire educational system, we had to overcome many difficulties at the beginning of this victorious trajectory.  For a year and a half, we operated in the form of a pilot program, when 429 selected schools in six Federation Units participated in this stage.  In June 2021, we opened the program to the voluntary and free membership of any public elementary school in the country.  Today, about two years after this national opening, our numbers have grown significantly.  Those 429 pioneering schools multiplied beyond 22 thousand, spread across all states and the Federal District, covering more than three thousand municipalities, which represent more than 54% of Brazilian cities.  Today, these schools add up to more than 5.6 million students enrolled, in addition to the almost 128 thousand education professionals registered on the Aprender Valor platform.  In a country with the continental dimensions of Brazil, we only achieved this jump in the numbers of Aprender Valor with the support of major partners, such as the National Union of Municipal Education Directors (Undime) and the National Council of Education Secretaries (Consed).  This leap would also not be possible without the involvement of State and Municipal Departments of Education, and without your engagement and enthusiasm.  Please receive our most sincere thanks for believing in this Program and for overcoming the difficulties to make a difference in the lives of each child and young person served.  However, we want more.  Throughout this year, we want not only the growth in the number of schools joined.  We also want to consolidate the growing and effective engagement of the schools already participating in the three main deliveries of the program: online training, school projects and assessments.  I want to highlight, among the novelties of Aprender Valor for 2023, the availability of 31 new projects on the Program's platform.  With the launch of these new projects, we have more than doubled the number of school projects available.  Thus, teachers will have many more options of topics and classes to apply in the classroom.  In addition, we had the adhesion of five new state secretariats to the Program.  Our welcome to the Seducs of Alagoas, Minas Gerais, Santa Catarina, Espirito Santo and Sergipe.  More than immense joy, we are sure that we are on the right path to bring free and quality financial education to our children and young people.  I thank all of you for believing in Learning Value and in the ability of Financial Education to multiply dreams.  I conclude by inviting those who are not yet part of Learning Value to join us. Memberships remain open throughout the year. Come also Learn Value.  I wish you all an excellent event!

Title: Speech by Mr. Renato Dias de Brito Gomes at the Economic Affairs Committee (CAE) of the Federal Senate. - 152.1 Kb
text: The CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL Brasilia, April 5, 2022. Statement by Mr. Renato Dias de Brito Gomes at the Hearing of the Committee on Economic Affairs (CAE) of the Federal Senate for consideration of his nomination to the position of Director of the Central Bank of Brazil Your Excellency Senator Otto Alencar, Chairman of the Committee on Economic Affairs; Your Excellency Senator Vanderlan Cardoso, Vice-President of the Committee on Economic Affairs; Your Excellency Senator Fernando Bezerra, rapporteur of the process that deals with the nomination of my name to the position of director of the Central Bank of Brazil; Your Excellencies Senators and Your Excellencies Senators, ladies and gentlemen, good morning. It is with great honor that I appear before this Commission after my nomination to the position of director of the Central Bank of Brazil, a position that I will hold with great pride and zeal if my name is approved by your excellencies and also by the plenary of the Federal Senate. I thank the President of the Republic and the President of the Central Bank of Brazil for the trust placed in me for the fulfillment of such an important mission. I hope to be up to such a challenge and will seek to serve the Brazilian population to the best of my abilities and with conscientious effort. As determined by the Central Bank autonomy law, approved in this House, it is up to the monetary authority to ensure price stability. Without prejudice to its fundamental objective, it must also ensure the stability and efficiency of the financial system, smooth fluctuations in the level of economic activity and promote full employment. These objectives will guide my performance as a member of the Central Bank's board of directors, if Your Excellencies deem it appropriate. I understand that my academic and professional trajectory qualifies me to exercise the function of Director of the Central Bank of Brazil. I have a bachelor's and master's degree in Economics from the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro; PhD in Economics from Northwestern University, in the United States, and Habilitation (or Habilitation) from the University of Toulouse Capitole, in France. Full Professor. I was a researcher at the French National Center for Scientific Research, of which I am now director of research. I was also a collaborator at the Center for Economic Policy Research, in the United Kingdom, of which I am now a permanent member. I have published several academic articles in highly prestigious international journals, as well as several publications at Computer Science conferences, articles in specialized Antitrust journals and book chapters. My main areas of academic research are Public Sector Economics and Industrial Economics, with an emphasis on Regulation of Means of Payment, Antitrust and Competition Defense. I supervised several doctoral theses and many master's dissertations. In 2018 I had my research project funded by a prestigious Starting Grant from the European Research Council with a budget of more than four million reais. During my academic career, I have always maintained intense contact with the private sector. I was a research economist at Google in the years following my doctorate, having helped design the auctions used in its ad exchange. I was a researcher hired by Banque Postale in France and BBVA bank in Spain, in both cases analyzing the regulation of means of payment. More recently, I conducted research work for Facebook in the area of antitrust and was a researcher funded by the Gates Foundation to conduct studies on interoperability in mobile payment methods in developing countries. I also provided consultancy to several companies in the area of payment methods in Europe and Brazil. I am convinced that my academic background and my professional career qualify me to perform the position of Director of the Central Bank of Brazil, if I am granted this honor by the Federal Senate. Brazil, Your Excellencies Senators, is in a moment of recovery after the health crisis, which took the lives and stole the bread of so many Brazilians. Several factors will determine our success. One of them is the proper functioning of financial intermediation, that is, the credit, payments and capital markets. The payments sector attracted the attention of Brazilians with the launch of Pix, an innovative instant payment method led by the Central Bank. This initiative has already generated enormous gains in efficiency and financial inclusion, and should continue to do so, probably reducing the aggregate cost of making and receiving payments in Brazil by percentage points of GDP. A similar effect is expected from open banking, or open financial system, in which each customer has the option of sharing their data with financial institutions, thus being able to choose, among several, the most advantageous credit offer. Information on the creditworthiness of customers is an essential input for the correct assessment of risks in financial transactions. Such data, however, were concentrated in large institutions. By allowing the sharing of this data, always with security and customer consent, open banking has the potential to expand competition in the financial system, expand the Brazilian credit market, and reduce the banking spread, a noble but elusive purpose of so many public policies. Such initiatives are also generators of inclusion, bringing financial intermediation to Brazilians who were previously deprived of the enormous potential of these services. This is only possible thanks to public policies that encourage innovation, reducing costs and favoring the entry of new competitors. I bring with me the belief, amply confirmed by recent experience, in the disruptive power of technology, which can serve as an inducer of unprecedented competition. to continue and deepen the Central Bank's competitive agenda, such as the evolutionary agendas of Pix and open banking. It must be recognized, however, that market mechanisms alone may not be sufficient to provide society with all the welfare gains that technological progress allows. Thus, after a market failure has been clearly identified, regulation may be necessary that aligns the private interests of economic agents with those of Brazilian society. Examples of this corrective action are the cases of the limits imposed on the interchange fee on the debit card and the ceiling on the interest rate on overdrafts. It is important to highlight that the action of the Central Bank, particularly in the credit and payment markets, greatly benefited from the valuable work, carried out in this House, of the Parliamentary Commission of Inquiry on cards. It is also worth mentioning the importance of regulatory outcome assessments, which confirm or invalidate ex post the regulator's presumption at the time of intervention. It is also important to ensure regulatory neutrality, understood as the design of rules that do not unduly favor one business model over another. Good regulation, however, does not imply complete uniformity of rules. On the contrary, different projects and organizational models must be regulated in proportion to the risk (or more generally) to the externality they impose on society as a whole. This is the objective, for example, of the Central Bank's rule that seeks to make the prudential requirements of different types of financial conglomerates proportional. The proper functioning of the financial system depends not only on regulation, but also on a vigilant, clear and predictable competition policy. The growing The complexity of business models, based on ecosystems that often combine marketplace functionalities with payment or even financial services, makes this task a challenge. Part of the difficulty comes from the Central Bank's perimeter of competence for competition matters, restricted to financial institutions. The intense coordination between the Central Bank and CADE, enshrined in a Memorandum of Understanding, has contributed to an effective joint action. This partnership, it is important to remember, has the fundamental support of this Noble House, which has already approved a bill that makes this framework permanent. If you see fit, I will make efforts to ensure that the competition policy that is the responsibility of the Central Bank follows a holistic approach, adapted to current business models, and that stimulates the offer of better - and cheaper - services to the customer of the financial system. I will also redouble my vigilance for mergers both horizontal (between competitors in the same market) and vertical (between companies in related markets). The latter can generate cross-ownership in complementary services markets, giving rise to predatory practices and barriers to the entry of new competitors. Last but certainly not least, it is necessary to preserve and ensure the stability of the financial system. I believe that there is no conflict between the achievement of this objective and the remarkable competitive dynamism that recent years have witnessed. I believe, however, that progress can still be made on many fronts, for example, by modernizing the law that deals with the authorization process for financial institutions. The review of this process will be beneficial by allowing the prudential action of the regulator to be effective and at the same time not prevent the emergence of new business models. We also need adequate tools to disconnect companies that fail from the financial system, without creating friction or contagion that threatens financial stability. To this end, the first step was taken with the submission to the Chamber of Deputies of PLP 281 of 2019, which deals with the bank resolution framework. This bill, if approved by Brazilian legislators, will allow the Central Bank to treat and liquidate problematic institutions in an agile and efficient manner, following international best practices. If I have the honor of being approved by Your Excellencies to compose the Board of Directors of the Central Bank, I want to commit myself to continue and deepen the work that has been developed in order to build a financial and payment system based on competition and innovation.
