Title: Speech by Director Renato Dias de Brito Gomes at the "Deep Dive Into Pix" Workshop.
text: A BANCO CENTRAL DO BRASIL Brasilia, 21 de novembro de 2022. Discurso do Diretor de Organizagao do Sistema Financeiro e Resolugao do Banco Central, Renato Dias de Brito Workshop Deep Dive Into Pix, organizado pelo Departamento de Competigao e de Estrutura do Mercado Financeiro (DECEM) e Departamento de Assuntos Internacionais (DERIN) Pagina 1 de 5 Good morning, everyone. It is a great pleasure to welcome you to this event to share our experience in developing Pix, a project that makes us so proud. Let me start by introducing myself. My name is Renato Gomes, and I am the Deputy Governor responsible for the area that, among other things, takes care of Pix regulatory aspects as well as of management and development of new features. Pix was developed from scratch by a small but incredibly efficient team at the Central Bank. This team deserves all the credit and the applause from the so many Brazilians that benefited from this innovation. The debate on instant payments at the Central Bank of Brazil began ten years ago. It became clear early on that an instant payment solution would be very much welcomed by Brazilian consumers. Brazilians love technology and the adoption and availability of smartphones is high. Moreover, the payment options available for Brazilians as recent as a bit more than 2 years ago were definitely behind the technological frontier. So, there was room for greater efficiency in the Brazilian payment system. Yet, the private sector had not developed a tool for instant payments. It is understandable that private actors did not enjoy the proper incentives to do so, as payment revenues would be jeopardized in exchange for a possible, but uncertain, market expansion. Moreover, developing from scratch an instant payment solution requires complex coordination and standard-setting activities. The need for an open architecture, fully interoperable, coupled with unbiased governance, are features that may fail to naturally flourish under private provision. For these reasons, the Central Bank of Brazil understood that instant payments should be part of a broad public policy agenda and its underlying infrastructure considered a public good. Accordingly, the development of Pix aimed at addressing market failures and complementing the existing payment means. From the start, we posited that Pix should be open, accessible, simple, and safe. We would like to share with you today the strategy we designed to connect these four characteristics. To overcome the challenge of a simple payment journey, we established a single logo that stated in small letters, besides the Pix image, Powered by Banco Central. Concomitantly, we prepared a user experience manual to standardize the offering of Pix by different institutions. Every institution must follow these rules when offering Pix. The idea here was to make sure that consumers understand there exists a public infrastructure behind the instant payment service offered by banks, and that all banks connect to the very same system when offering instant payments. That any bank can join, all under equal conditions, renders Pix an open scheme. We believe that, by virtue of being open and standardized across Pagina 2 de 5 By design, no one would need to download apps or register on new websites to use Pix. Consumers could use the apps of their own banks, which were already known and trusted. In other words, Pix was born integrated in the daily lives of people and companies. In addition, being offered as a service by Payment Service Providers within their own applications, Pix inherited the application's security systems, which had already been extensively tested. This helps making Pix a safe payment method. In addition to instantaneity, Pix has other attractive features. It provides a comprehensive, cost-free, and non-bureaucratic payment mechanism for both payers and payees; it does not demand machines, software, or new applications. It is enough to have a cell phone or internet banking. This helps making Pix accessible. Once the supply strategy was defined, the next step was to think about distribution. As a regulator of the financial system, the Central Bank determined that the largest institutions in terms of the number of transactional accounts must offer Pix. With the largest institutions offering Pix, the other institutions followed suit, so as not to lose customers. As a result, from day one, virtually every Brazilian could make or receive a Pix. The other supporting pillar of Pix is its infrastructure. The goal was to have it accessible, neutral on competitive grounds, and low-cost. To make sure these objectives were attained, the Central Bank built it in-house. We adopted a cost- recovery approach, charging only BRL 0.01 for every ten Pix transactions to the receiving institution (about USD 0.01 for every 50 transactions). At the same time, as the scheme owner, the Central Bank determined to PSPs that transactions between individuals would be free of charge. When they involved firms, consumers would still have it for free, but firms could be charged by the payment provider. This fee structure made sure that consumers would quickly be on board, rendering Pix a must-adopt for firms. This strategy solves the coordination (or chicken-and-egg) problem inherent to industries that exhibit network effects. Two other factors help understanding Pix success. The first was that in 2012 we built a legal framework creating a new type of authorized institution with a lighter prudential requirement, proportional to the risk. It was the origin of the payment (as opposed to financial) institutions in Brazil. The former cannot grant loans but can offer prepaid and credit cards. These institutions became popular in Brazil, notably by offering free-of-charge accounts and user-friendly technology. All services are offered through smartphones, with no need to visit physical branches. The expansion of these institutions put competitive pressure on incumbents, who soon responded with Pagina 3 de 5 similar offerings. Accordingly, when Pix was launched, the use of cell phones for financial transactions was already widespread. The second factor is that we launched Pix in November 2020. We were in the middle of the Pandemic, and the digitization imposed by social distancing policies had changed the habits of many Brazilians, who incorporated the advantages of mobile technology into their daily lives. Social media played a prominent role in this period, either as a mean of communication or as a marketplace. Instantaneity became an intrinsic feature of this process, as a gratifying experience doing business is essential in the digital world. During this Pandemic, more than 93% of Brazilian municipalities had 4G coverage. In addition, around 90% of people in the income classes D and E; and 58% of those in class C used the internet exclusively via smartphones. In addition, the Brazilian government paid the emergency aid through digital accounts provided by a public bank. Approximately 14 million unbanked people were inserted into the Brazilian financial system through this program, with 10 million only in the period from May to July 2020 alone, the peak of the expansion of emergency aid. The launch of Pix during this period was the missing piece for accelerating this digitization process. Brazilians incorporated Pix quickly. Less than a year later, in August 2021, more than half of the Brazilian population had made at least one Pix. Last month, October 2022, more than 138 million users were registered in Pix - about 64% of the Brazilian population. These users performed more than 2.5 billion transactions in one month. A year ago, in October 2021, there were 1.1 billion monthly transactions. We more than doubled the use of Pix during this period! A significant percentage of Pix usage is among individuals, but its usage in business is also noteworthy. In particular, micro-entrepreneurs and self- employed workers have widely adopted this means of payment. According to data from Sebrae (Brazilian Micro and Small Business Support Service), Pix became the main mean of payment for 51% of self-employed workers and 28% of micro and small entrepreneurs. A recent survey also reveals that Pix has become the primary means of payment on Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter Platforms.1. Although Pix is only two years old, these are significant numbers! Many other possibilities for developing products and services based on Pix are being explored. The next frontier right now is using Pix through payment initiators connected to the Central Banks Open Finance initiative. We are also in the process of developing Pix Automatico, which will enable consumers to automatize recurrent payments. Importantly, consumers can use this service from any PSP participating on Pix, and not only from the banks (typically the large ones) who have a bilateral agreement with the payee firm. This 1 - levantamento/ Pagina 4 de 5 feature will level the playing field across large and small banks, intensifying competition in the banking sector. In addition, we are closely following the development of Buy Now, Pay Later services based on Pix. More broadly, we see Pix as part of a large eco-system that will bring together instant payments, our Open Finance initiative and our CBDC initiative. In the future, we hope, consumers will seamlessly get quotes for financial services through Open Banking, make instant payments through Pix and enjoy the programmability and composability features of the Real Digital. Technology will eliminate informational asymmetries and bring down competitive barriers. It is precisely the practical aspects of this adventure that we want to share with you today. We have here today around 30 institutions, including central banks, financial regulators and international organizations. It is an honor and a privilege to share our technical knowledge and experience with such a qualified audience. We see the collaboration with other countries as a great opportunity to promote public policy on instant payments around the world. This collaboration also opens the door to the development of instant cross-border payments. Connecting domestic instant payment systems is certainly one possible avenue to this end. It remains however a lot of work to be done in harmonizing regulation, technology and operations across different payment systems. We intend to share technology, of course. But we also want to share our vision of how instant payments can be applied to mitigate frictions, complement the existing payment frameworks, and achieve financial inclusion. In doing so, we will be working to promote efficient, secure, and inclusive financial and payment systems, which is our mandate. I want to take this opportunity to thank one more time the Pix team and all of you who give us the privilege of your company and your expertise. I hope this collaboration is a first step towards a future of efficient and cheap cross-border payments. Have a great day and I hand the floor over to Angelo, who is the head of the area responsible for managing Pix. Thank you very much. Pagina 5 de 5

Title: Remarks by President Roberto Campos Neto at the opening of the Laboratory of Financial and Technological Innovations - LIFT Day 2022, broadcast on the Central Bank's YouTube Channel. - 179.3 Kb
text: CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL Brasilia (DF), March 22, 2022. Notes by the President of the Central Bank of Brazil, Roberto Campos Neto LIFT DAY 2022 Good morning everyone, and thank you for attending Lift Day 2022. Introduction  The Laboratory of Financial and Technological Innovations (LIFT) is an innovation program created in 2018 in a partnership between the Central Bank (BC) and Fenasbac.  The program is based on the assumption that in order to advance in the innovation of the Brazilian financial system, we need to establish a collaborative environment between the Central Bank and the private sector (which includes regulated institutions, startups, and technology providers).  As part of the BC# Agenda, LIFT focuses on fostering innovative solutions to prepare the financial system for a technological and inclusive future, working as an inducer of innovation.  Among the initiatives that make up the LIFT program, I highlight: o The LIFT Lab, an environment where entrepreneurs submit project proposals aligned with the BC# Agenda, for an acceleration of innovative projects, with the support of technology partners. o LIFT Learning, a partnership between universities, development agencies and private companies focused on applied research, involving undergraduate and graduate students, for the development of innovative solutions for sponsoring companies. o I also highlight the LIFT Challenge, launched in November last year.  This is a special edition of the LIFT Lab, focusing on the acceleration of technologies within a specific theme.  The edition of the LIFT Challenge is underway with a focus on the development of the Digital Real, the digital currency issued by the Central Bank.  This initiative involves the participation of companies operating in the financial sector interested in building minimum viable products based on the Digital Real.  The objective of this first challenge, for which 9 projects were selected, will be to evaluate the potential use cases of the Digital Real.  The LIFT program also includes: o The periodical journal LIFT Papers, with articles focused on financial technological innovations and the results of each of the projects developed in LIFT; and o LIFTTalks, which are interviews and webinars promoted by Fenasbacon financial technological innovations, bringing together professionals from the Central Bank and the private sector.  The event we held today, LIFT Day, aims to present to Brazilian society the results of the last edition of LIFT Lab and promote a debate with technology partners on relevant topics of the innovation agenda for the financial sector. The road already traveled and what lies ahead  Since its first edition, LIFT Lab has accelerated more than 60 new projects for society. o Some of these projects have received investments from the private sector and today have become products in use by citizens and companies.  The relevant results presented made LIFT Lab recognized in 2019 as the best Sanbox and acceleration initiative among central banks around the world.  In 2021, the 4 edition of LIFT Lab took place, which received the registration of 43 projects, including from abroad. o This issue demonstrates the interest of the private sector in collaborating with the Central Bank in favor of innovations that can bring real benefits to Brazilian citizens.  As you will see, the projects in this edition were focused on inclusion and financial education solutions, within the Open Finance proposal. o In the theme of financial inclusion, there was a proposal for new credit models, using technologies such as Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence. o In the field of financial education, solutions were proposed to improve the management of personal finances.  In addition, there are innovative projects focused on: o in the granting of rural credit; o in the purchase and sale of assets using DLT technology; and o in the use of Artificial Intelligence to build new fraud prevention models within PIX. Closure  I would like to give special thanks to our partners who make their technologies and knowledge available to proponents in favor of the development of innovations for the financial system. o I thank the companies: Amazon Web Service; Celer; Cielo; IBM; Microsoft; Multiledgers; Oracle; RTM; R3 Rope; and o To the Fenasbac Institute.  Finally, I would like to invite companies and entrepreneurs to continue collaborating with us in building the financial system of the future. o Without this partnership between Central Bank, technology companies and the financial sector, it would not be possible to deliver valuable innovations to our society. Thank you very much.

Title: Remarks by President Roberto Campos Neto at the opening of the Global Carbon Market - Decarbonization and Green Investments Congress, promoted by Banco do Brasil and Petrobras. - 240.6 Kb
text: Bras92lia (DF), May 18, 2022. Notes by the President of the Central Bank of Brazil, Roberto Campos Neto, at the Opening Plenary of the Global Carbon Market, Decarbonization and Green Investments Congress Participants: Joaquim Leite (Minister of the Environment) Fausto de Andrade Ribeiro (President of Banco do Brasil) Jos8e Mauro Ferreira Coelho (President of Petrobras) Roberto Campos Neto (President of the Central Bank) a5 Good morning everyone! a5 I would like to start by greeting: o The Minister of the Environment, Joaquim Leite; o The President of Banco do Brasil, Fausto de Andrade Ribeiro; and o The President of Petrobras, Jos8e Mauro Ferreira Coelho. Introduction a5 It is a great pleasure to participate in this event. o The environmental issue is an extremely important topic that arouses great interest in society. o It is also a relevant topic for policymakers, business people, producers, investors, etc.; o In this context, the development of the carbon market imposes great challenges, but also generates enormous opportunities; This is particularly true in the case of Brazil, a country with enormous environmental potential. Carbon Credit Market: a5 The carbon credit market is an ingenious way to internalize externalities. Page 2 of 11 o It enables each country to internalize the benefits of reducing its own emissions, contributing to greater cooperation. a5 The global carbon credit market had been in a process of growth, but after the 2008 financial crisis, it retracted. a5 Subsequently, the market began to recover, due to the recovery of the global economy and the demand for a more sustainable economy. a5 The development of this market has advanced, and has great growth potential, due to: o The maturation of society in relation to environmental issues ; o The increase in the strictness of countries' environmental regulations; and o The fact that the scope of pricing is not yet broad. Climate Issues Influencing Process a5 The development of the carbon market is part of the long process of maturation of society in terms of climate issues . a5 This process took place in stages: Page 3 of 11 o The 1st stage consisted of the demand for clean energy production (clean matrix). o The 2nd stage in food production respecting the environment (clean agriculture). o The 3rd stage is characterized by investors with governance policies for the environmental issue, among which we can mention investment funds and the financial market in general. a5 This third wave is the most important. Importance of the environmental issue for the Central Bank a5 At the Central Bank of Brazil (BC), we are aware of the growing concerns about sustainable development, as well as social, environmental, and climate risks. a5 The environmental and climate issue, which has long been a topic of great importance on the international agenda, has gained even more significant momentum after the Covid-19 pandemic. o With society increasingly demanding that the recovery be sustainable and inclusive. a5 In the case of central banks, this agenda is important because sustainability-related issues have the potential to affect their two main missions: o Monetary policy and financial stability. Page 4 of 11 a5 In the recent period, for example, we have witnessed several adverse climate shocks with negative impacts on inflation. o Heat waves, frosts, droughts, and other events have affected food and energy prices, with significant impacts on Brazilian inflation. a5 In the long run, these shocks can have lasting effects. o Affecting productivity and long-term economic growth . a5 To deal with these questions, we need to stay at the frontier of knowledge and action, answering: o The evolution of society's demands; o Structural changes in the economy; and o To shocks and risks, present and future. Central Bank's sustainability agenda a5 The Central Bank has a long history of supporting the environmental agenda, implementing measures related to the subject, and actively participating in the international debate. o Over the last decade, the Central Bank has issued several regulations related to the environmental issue. Page 5 of 11 a5 In September 2020, the Central Bank launched its sustainability agenda as an additional pillar of its strategic agenda for the development of the financial system, the BC# Agenda. a5 The launch of the BC# Sustainability Agenda aims to: o Lead by example within SFN; and o Deliver concrete results to society, in line with international best practices. a5 When the Sustainability Dimension was launched, the Central Bank established a set of concrete measures outlined in five major themes: regulation; supervision; development of policies and instruments; establishment of partnerships; and actions of an internal nature. a5 I would now like to mention examples of actions from our sustainable agenda, some already delivered and others still in progress. Partnerships a5 The Central Bank has already formalized several partnerships, such as: o A ades8bo 88 Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS). o The signing of a memorandum of understanding with the Climate Bonds Initiative (CBI). Page 6 of 11 o Participation in technical cooperation with the German Society for International Cooperation (GIZ) in the project Sustainable Brazilian Finance (FIBraS). a5 Partnerships are very important because they bring a number of benefits, such as: o Exchange of experiences and knowledge about best practices in socio-environmental issues; o Improvement in Analysis of data and mitigation of risks socio-environmental in the financial system; and or Strengthening of the relationship with other central banks and international organizations. Supervision a5 In the area of supervision, there were: o Greater structuring and expansion of the collection of information on social, environmental and climate risks; as well as o Carrying out stress tests for climate risks. * With the inclusion of climate risk scenarios in new and improved stress tests carried out by the Central Bank, in line with international best practices. Internal actions a5 Among the actions of an internal nature of the Central Bank we have: Page 7 of 11 o The inclusion of social, environmental and climate aspects in the BC's Integrated Risk Management. o The launch, in September 2021, of the first "Report on Social, Environmental and Climate Risks and Opportunities ", with the Central Bank being one of the first central banks in the world to do something similar; and o The creation, in December 2021, of the Sustainable Economy Committee (ECOS) of the Central Bank. Policies and instruments a5 In this regard, it is worth highlighting the inclusion of sustainability criteria for the selection of counterparties in the management of international reserves and for the selection of investments. Regulation a5 In the area of regulation, the Central Bank has sought to dialogue with society through public consultations. a5 In March and April 2021, the Central Bank launched public consultation notices, which dealt with several actions on the sustainability agenda. o Among the actions addressed, we can highlight the improvement of the regulation on socio-environmental risks. a5 The final proposal approved by the CMN: Page 8 of 11 o Improves the definitions of social risk, environmental risk, and climate risks (physical and transitional). o It integrates these risks into the framework already established for the management of other traditional risks, such as credit, market, liquidity and operational. o It establishes criteria for the identification, measurement, evaluation, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation of adverse effects resulting from the interaction between these risks. o Extends the regulatory requirements applicable to the management of traditional risks to social, environmental and climate-related risks ; and o Improves the requirements for the implementation of actions aimed at the effectiveness of the Social, Environmental and Climate Responsibility Policy (PRSAC), with the strengthening of the governance structure and the requirements for the disclosure of information to the external public. Bureau of Sustainable Rural Credit (Green Bureau) a5 One of the proposals under development deals with the implementation of the Sustainable Rural Credit Bureau. o Guided by the principles of Open Finance, it aims to allow beneficiaries of rural credit to provide information Page 9 of 11 registered in the system to any interested party, without the need for intermediation by financial agents. o The Bureau will be a tool for risk management by financial institutions and an important step towards the development of a green bond market, as well as for the securitization of these green credit operations. o Providing information to financial markets will allow for better asset pricing. o In the area of public policy, the Bureau will allow policymakers to also use registration information to grant additional incentives for sustainable rural projects. Conclusion a5 To conclude, I would like to emphasize that the objective of this agenda is, within the mandate of the Central Bank, to create the conditions for the development of sustainable finance in the SFN with a view to: o International best practices related to sustainable finance . o Greater availability of resources from the financial system for sustainable enterprises. o Better risk management social, environmental and Climate. Page 10 of 11 a5 This set of measures is extensive, but by no means exhaustive. a5 We need to advance further, and the plan is to remain at the frontier of knowledge and actions to address social, environmental and climate challenges, since this is an area in constant evolution. a5 Thank you very much Page 11 of 11

Title: President Roberto Campos Neto's live remarks on the modernization of Complementary Law 130/2009, promoted by OCB.
text: CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL Brasilia-DF, August 30, 2022 Notes by the President of the Central Bank of Brazil, Roberto Campos Neto, for the Special Live - Enactment of Complementary Law 196/2022  Good afternoon everyone.  I would like to thank you for the invitation to participate in this ceremony and to greet the president of the OCB System, Mr. Marcio de Freitas, Senator Vanderlan Cardoso, deputies Arnaldo Jardim and Evair de Melo, other authorities, and all those who follow us online.  For me it is a satisfaction to be present at this event, which celebrates the enactment of Complementary Law 196, bringing relevant improvements to Complementary Law 130, the legal framework of credit cooperativism.  This law is the result of intense work promoted by several agents of the National Cooperative Credit System (SNCC) and the Central Bank of Brazil.  By updating and modernizing the regulatory framework of cooperativism, the new law contributes to cooperatives being able to continue operating in an environment of profound transformation, in which competitiveness, innovation and technology are increasingly present.  As you know, cooperativism is highlighted in our BC# Agenda, which demonstrates the importance that the Central Bank gives to the segment.  If we go through the various dimensions of the BC# Agenda, we can see that cooperativism is linked to all of them, given its enormous contribution to the development of a more competitive, more inclusive, more sustainable and more efficient financial system.  The renewal of the legal framework is part of the efforts made by the Central Bank to contribute to the development of the sector, focusing on three strategic axes:  foster activities and businesses;  improve management and governance; and  improve the systemic organization and efficiency of the National Cooperative Credit System.  The changes introduced will certainly allow cooperatives to have better conditions to exercise and expand their business, for the benefit of their members and their communities.  We know that the benefits brought by credit cooperativism go beyond the Financial System.  It is never too much to emphasize the role that cooperatives play in the development of the communities in which they are inserted, positively impacting multiple variables, such as income, employment and entrepreneurship.  It is also worth remembering that the surplus financial result of its activities is returned and distributed among the cooperative members, which provides a return for their communities, for the benefit of all.  In addition, cooperatives drive financial inclusion and education, often reaching remote locations with less presence of the traditional financial system.  The participation of members in the management of cooperatives is a factor in the formation of financial awareness.  We have repeatedly observed that the growth of the sector is above other segments of the National Financial System (SFN), with relevant growth in Assets, Credit Portfolio and Deposits.  The cooperative sector has been gaining relevance as a credit provider to its members, notably individuals and micro, small and medium-sized companies.  By way of illustration, in June 2022, the twelve-month growth of the credit portfolio of the National Cooperative Credit System reached 29%, while the growth of the SFN as a whole was 17% in the same period. o And the most important thing is that this growth takes place in a consistent and structured way.  If much has already been done, with quality and consistency, we cannot lose sight of the opportunities and challenges that present themselves. Recent innovations, such as Open-Finance, the Sandbox, Pix, and the digitalization of financial services, represent trends and even more opportunities for credit unions.  For all these reasons, we have great expectations regarding the development of credit unions in the coming years.  The enactment of Complementary Law 196 represents an important step in this successful trajectory.  We will continue to work in harmony to give concreteness to the changes introduced and we expect a significant expansion of the activities of the credit union, with an even more solid presence in an increasingly developed financial market. Thank you very much.

Title: Notes by President Roberto Campos Neto at the 2022 Leaders of Brazil Award, promoted by the Lide Group.
text: Notes from President Roberto Campos Neto to thank the Leaders of Brazil Award 2022 Sao Paulo-SP, 07/12/2022 - 21:30h Good evening everyone!  It is a great satisfaction to be here and a great honor to receive, on behalf of the Central Bank of Brazil (BC), the 2022 Leaders of Brazil award, which seeks to recognize the commitment of leaders with the objective of making Brazil a better and more competitive country.  Throughout my presentation, I intend to highlight some important actions of the Central Bank that gave rise to this award, and talk a little about future actions in our technology agenda.  As I am in the Copom's quiet period, I will not address issues related to the current and future macroeconomic context. Economic retrospective Pandemic and economic consequences  In the last 3 years, we have experienced a very big change in several paradigms of the global economy. This change had already been occurring for years in a moderate and silent way. o The pandemic accelerated the process.  At the beginning of the pandemic, countries thought there would be a great depression.  For this reason, governments implemented the largest program to sustain the economy in history.  The effect of this coordinated work meant that the initial forecast did not come true. o The predicted Great Depression turned into a mild recession.  Economists and policymakers have had great difficulty understanding the economic effects of such a large and globally coordinated movement.  Demand policies, together with other factors, generated a large imbalance between the goods and services sectors.  In addition, the increase in demand for goods has generated a large increase in the demand for energy for the production of goods. Capex in the energy sectors did not react to prices.  On the goods supply side, goods markets have not been able to react quickly to the increase in demand.  The supply did not react as expected due to a series of changes (cracks) that were already occurring in the world. o Reduced productivity with low appetite for structural reforms. o Changes in demography and the labor market. o Disruptions in global chains and deviations from the model of comparative advantages, o Reduction in cooperation in technology.  This implies less adaptability in the offer.  The result of this whole process was the increase in inflation at a global level. War between Russia vs. Russia Ukraine: Economic consequences  The war between Russia and Ukraine has accelerated these trends.  Governments have responded with new packages of measures to address rising food and energy prices.  The overriding question is how to do this efficiently.  The literature suggests the 3 Ts (Targeted, Tailored and Temporary) model o There is great difficulty with each of these "Ts". Agenda BC#  After this retrospective view of the global scenario, I would like to talk a little about our reform agenda for the National Financial System (SFN), and what we think about the future.  Over the past few years, the Central Bank has been implementing several initiatives on this agenda. o In the months and years to come, we will have much more, with the integration of projects that initially started separately, but will now be increasingly integrated. o Greater inclusion; o Lower intermediation cost; o More competition, with reduced barriers to entry; o Efficiency in risk control; o Data monetization; and o Complete tokenization of financial assets and contracts. Title: Remarks by President Roberto Campos Neto at the ceremony for the delivery of the "Brazil-Spain Personality Award".
text: CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL Notes by President Roberto Campos Neto at the ceremony of the " Brazil-Spain Personality Award", promoted by the Official Spanish Chamber of Commerce in Brazil and the Spanish Embassy. Brasilia, 13/12/2022,19:30h - 23:30h Introduction  It is a great satisfaction to be here and a great honor to receive, on behalf of the Central Bank of Brazil (BC), the Brazil-Spain Personality award.  I would like to congratulate Ambassador Fernando Garcia Casas, the other honoree of this evening, who was also awarded this honor. Economic scenario  Before talking about the Brazilian conjuncture, I would like to contextualize the economic process that has been taking place in recent years. o To understand the great challenges that the country faces, it is necessary to go back a little to the beginning of the pandemic to understand the global context. Pandemic and economic consequences  In the last 3 years, we have experienced a very big change in several paradigms of the global economy. This change had already been occurring for years in a moderate and silent way. o The pandemic accelerated the process.  At the beginning of the pandemic, countries thought there would be a great depression.  For this reason, governments implemented the largest program to sustain the economy in history.  The effect of this coordinated work meant that the initial forecast did not come true. o The predicted Great Depression turned into a mild recession.  Economists and policymakers have had great difficulty understanding the economic effects of such a large and globally coordinated movement.  Demand policies, together with other factors, generated a large imbalance between the goods and services sectors.  In addition, the increase in demand for goods has generated a large increase in the demand for energy for the production of goods. Capex in the energy sectors did not react to prices.  On the goods supply side, goods markets have not been able to react quickly to the increase in demand.  The supply did not react as expected due to a series of changes (cracks) that were already occurring in the world. o Reduced productivity with low appetite for structural reforms. o Changes in demography and the labor market. o Disruptions in global chains and deviations from the model of comparative advantages, o Reduction in cooperation in technology.  This implies less adaptability in the offer.  The result of this whole process was the increase in inflation at a global level. War between Russia vs. Russia Ukraine: Economic consequences  The war between Russia and Ukraine has accelerated these trends.  Governments have responded with new packages of measures to address rising food and energy prices.  The overriding question is how to do this efficiently.  The literature suggests the 3 Ts (Targeted, Tailored and Temporary) model o There is great difficulty with each of these "Ts". Brazilian conjuncture  Having outlined this global background, let's now talk about the economic situation in Brazil.  In general, I would like to draw attention to some important elements. o The reforms carried out in recent years have produced effects to strengthen supply. Example: Labour market o Reduction in subsidized credit contributed to reducing the neutral rate, benefiting the allocation of resources and expansion of markets. o The Central Bank quickly identified the negative effects of the pandemic.  Measures to expand liquidity and release capital. o The Central Bank quickly identified the permanent nature of inflation.  It started the monetary tightening cycle in a timely manner.  We have an ongoing movement to reduce inflation. Economic growth in 2022 has been above initial expectations for the year.  The median of current market agents' projections for 2022 indicates growth close to 3%.  For 2023, there are expectations of lower growth.  An important element of the domestic situation is the fiscal issue. o A cohesive plan is needed, with fiscal coherence and continuity of structural reforms.  Policies that reconcile meeting social demands with fiscal sustainability.  Implementation of a structural reform agenda.  This will ensure sustainable growth, with inflation and low interest rates.  Brazil is a strong candidate to benefit from the new global scenario. the country has a large labor market and consumer market. o Enormous capacity to produce renewable energy and food.  The country can help in the world's food and energy security. Inflation outlook  As I have already mentioned, the pandemic and more recently the invasion of Ukraine have caused inflation to become higher and more persistent at a global level.  Brazil had important challenges in the evolution of post-pandemic inflation:  The Central Bank started its monetary tightening cycle before the other countries, in March 2021. This timely reaction was largely due to: o Our initial perception of the nature of current inflation; o Our assessment of the costs related to the actions of central banks; and o The fact that inflation in Brazil started to increase earlier than in other jurisdictions.  The monetary tightening strategy is beginning to bear fruit. o In the 12 months ended in November 2022, the IPCA registered 5.9%, while the average of the cores is at 9.4%.  However, more recently, we have observed a deceleration movement in prices.  Looking ahead, inflation should continue to decelerate. o The median of market expectations for 2022 and 2023 is 5.8% and 5.1%, respectively, still above the targets. o For the following years the agents project:  3,5% for 2024;  3,0% for 2025; and  3,0% for 2026. o The Central Bank projects inflation of 6.0% for 2022 and 5.0% for 2023 (December Copom). Monetary policy  At its last meeting, the Monetary Policy Committee (Copom) decided to keep the Selic rate at 13.75% p.a.  The Committee will remain vigilant, assessing whether the strategy of maintaining the basic interest rate for a sufficiently prolonged period will be able to ensure the convergence of inflation. disinflation, as well as the anchoring of expectations around their targets. Agenda BC#  I would now like to talk a little about our reform agenda for the National Financial System (SFN), and what we think about the future.  Over the past few years, the Central Bank has been implementing several initiatives on this agenda. o In the months and years to come, we will have much more, with the integration of projects that initially started separately, but will now be increasingly integrated.  We have a complete agenda for the digitalization of financial intermediation, whose objectives are: o Greater inclusion; o Lower intermediation cost; o More competition, with reduced barriers to entry; o Efficiency in risk control; o Data monetization; and o Complete tokenization of financial assets and contracts. Four fundamental blocks  The four fundamental blocks of this integrated agenda are the following projects, with their respective elements:  Internationalization of the currency and opening of capital markets o Enable a more efficient cross-border payment system.  Universal payment system (Pix) o Wide use by the population o Cheap, fast, secure, transparent and inclusive system o Programmable  Open Finance o Data standardization o Inclusion of all products o Security - Standardization o Reduced cost of sharing  Real digital (CBDC) o Bridge to the De-Fi environment, linking the banking system to the digital world o Introduce tokenization concept (broad-based) o Reduction of physical currency o Increased banking efficiency  Risk control  Liquidation  Data analysis  Financing  Goods o Data monetization  Interaction of tokens with digital wallet o Competition by channel, not just by product Phases of the block integration process  From now on we will have an organized process of integration of these projects, which will take place in the following phases:  Pix e Open Finance o Payment Initiator  Pix and other products o Ex.: Credit via Pix etc. o We are taking steps towards a future integration of domestic systems of Instant payouts.  Pix e Real digital (CBDC) o Digital wallet and non-digital wallet  Real digital (CBCD) e Open Finance o Tokenization and portability of tokens  Financial aggregator o Competition by channel, and no longer just by product  Construction of the digital wallet Financial Aggregator  In our vision of the future, it is unreasonable to expect people to have to deal with different applications to access information and services from different financial institutions.  In fact, people will be able to choose a single application that will integrate information and services from different financial institutions.  In addition to serving as a digital wallet, this application will make it possible to make payments, investments, transfers and asset purchases; perform cash management; and acquire many other financial services from different institutions.  This process is already underway, but we will work to accelerate it even more in the coming years.  In conclusion, I would like to wish you all an excellent dinner and thank you once again for this award.  Thank you very much!

text: Apontamentos para o 2023 Milken South Florida Dialogues Miami, 07/02/2023 Introduction  We are experiencing a period of unprecedented technological innovation in the financial system. o In today's digital world, people are looking for ways to represent anything that might have value in a digital format. o To this end, encrypted assets have been distributed on a ledger so that they become verifiable, transferable, and divisible. o This process of asset tokenization allows us to extract, in digital form, value from different types of assets, such as photos, art, properties, ideas and money. Even virtual reality (VR) is being tokenized.  This innovation process suggests that we are moving towards an increasingly tokenized economy, in which the negotiation of tokenized assets is the main transformation. o In the financial system, this process tends to lead to a growing dichotomy between what is account-based and what is token-based on banks' balance sheets. o Ultimately, these developments may lead to the creation of global, regulated, token-based and multi-asset networks. Agenda BC#  It is within this context of innovation that the Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) has sought to promote its agenda of financial innovations - the Agenda BC#. o We have implemented over the last few years several innovation projects of our agenda of structural reforms for the financial system, such as: The instant payments system (Pix); and Open Finance. o In addition, we have other projects underway, such as: The modernization of foreign exchange (FX) legislation; and The Digital Real (central bank digital currency or CBDC). Pagina 2 de 7 The goal is to make the Brazilian National Financial System more efficient and modern and to promote the democratization of financial services through technology.  To date, Pix, the BCB's instant payment system launched in 2020, has far exceeded our expectations, and its use continues to increase month after month. o Since 2020, many new features have been added to Pix. o For instance, making payments on due dates or on a scheduled basis is now possible. o It is also possible to withdraw cash from a retailer, which enormously increases the capillarity of the withdrawal service. o Furthermore, new accessibility and safety mechanisms are already in operation.  Even with all these new features, various other innovations will come along. o In the future, customers will be able to acquire some financial services currently available on the banking channel, as credit, using Pix. o Programmable operations with Pix will also be possible. o We also expect interconnections involving Pix and other instant payment systems, enabling Pix for international payments. Open Finance  The Brazilian Open Finance environment is defined as the sharing of data, products, and services between regulated entities  financial institutions, payment institutions and other entities licensed by the BCB  at the customer's discretion. o This initiative is expected to enhance the efficiency of Brazil's credit and payment markets by promoting a more inclusive and competitive financial system. Pagina 3 de 7 o Open Finance celebrates two years with 15 million customers, 22 million customer data-sharing consents, and more than 800 participations institutions. o This project has been implemented in phases. o For 2023, it is expected that the participating institutions will start: Offering the sharing of data on new groups of products and services, such as investment, insurance, pension plans and foreign exchange; and Promoting improvements in the data sharing and payment initiation journey. Foreign exchange legislation  The modernization of foreign-exchange legislation, in turn, will improve the business environment in Brazil. o It resulted from the passage of a new law by the National Congress of Brazil in late 2021. o The new regulatory framework will facilitate the insertion of Brazilian companies into international markets and increase the attractiveness of the Brazilian economy to foreign capital. Brazilian CBDC and projects integration  In the coming months and years, this innovation process will lead to a financial system in which competition will be not only by product but also by channel.  This process will bring together all four projects: Pix, Open Finance, the internationalization of our currency and the Digital Real. o We envision these four building blocks giving rise to financial aggregators, allowing customers to access information and services from different banks using the same applications. Pagina 4 de 7  This integration will serve as the basis for establishing our digital currency. o We believe that the benefits of a CBDC go far beyond improvements in wholesale and cross-border payments or enabling instant payments. o Our view is that a CBDC is an important driver of new business models and innovation in the financial system. o The challenge for the Digital Real is to enable uses beyond the payment solutions available today.  The Digital Real will promote the provision of financial services based on tokenized deposits. o The principle will be to transform deposits into tokens (stablecoins), which can be held by the public and have an equivalent value to a CBDC held by financial institutions and issued by the BCB. o The fact that banks will be the issuers of tokenized deposits will avoid financial disintermediation and problems on their balance sheets. o As the Digital Real will not be interest-bearing, it will not interfere directly in monetary-policy transmission or the macroeconomic framework. o At the same time, tokenized deposits will have the same regulatory principles as conventional deposits, ensuring the security of the financial system.  Furthermore, the Digital Real is expected to enable a more efficient trading chain of tokenized assets, strengthening the migration to a token-based world. o It happens because the same technology developed by banks and payment institutions to tokenize deposits can be used to tokenize a diverse number of other assets. o Other positive outcomes include using new technologies to enhance banks' internal controls and settlement processes. Pagina 5 de 7 execution of projects on the CBDC use cases proposed by banks, payment institutions and other market participants, involving solutions for: o Delivery versus payment (DvP); o Payment versus payment (PvP); o Internet of things (loT); and o Decentralized finance (DeFi), among others.  Our idea is to start a pilot project in 2023, and if everything goes as planned, the Brazilian CBDC could be up and running by late 2024 or the beginning of 2025. Data Monetization  Data monetization is another important issue in our agenda. o Today, it is very difficult for users of the financial system to monetize their data, o As owners of their information, they should be able to do that. o We work to create ways to allow them to monetize their information in the future.  In this sense, the financial aggregator could also be used as a data wallet, where the user could store data and choose the best way to monetize it. o For this, we need to track which data can flow in an organized and secure way. View of the Future  In our view of the future, it is unreasonable to expect that people will have to handle many different apps to access information and services from different financial institutions.  Our concept is to have an integrated process that allows people to choose a single app that integrates information and services from distinct players.  In addition to serving as a digital wallet, this app will make it possible to make payments, investments, transfers and asset purchases; conduct cash management; and acquire many other financial services from different institutions. Pagina 6 de 7  This aggregator would allow both online and offline transactions. The integration process  The integration process of all these projects has a timeline with the following phases: 1. Pix and Open Finance: Payment initiator. 2. Pix and other products: Ex.: Credit etc. 3. Pix and currency internationalization. 4. Pix and Digital Real (CBDC): Digital wallet and non-digital wallet. 5. Digital Real (CBCD) and Open Finance. 6. Financial aggregator: Competition for channel. 7. Build of a digital wallet. Conclusion  Technological evolution has been one of the greatest BCB allies to ensure a more efficient financial system and to promote the democratization of financial services.  In this sense, technology is one of the most effective instruments we have to reach these goals and design the financial system of the future. Pagina 7 de 7

Title: Remarks by President Roberto Campos Neto at the Seminar "25 years of Law No. 9,613/1998 - Evolution of the Brazilian AML/FPT System", promoted by Coaf. - 201.2 Kb
text: CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL Brasilia (DF), December 4, 2023. Notes by the President of the Central Bank of Brazil, Roberto Campos Neto Seminar of 25 years of Law No. 9.613, of 1998  I would like to start by greeting the participants of this event:  Rafael Bezerra Ximenes de Vasconcelos, substitute president of Coaf;  Raja Kumar, President Do Ghauffy;  Bruno Caiado de Acioli, representing the Attorney General's Office;  Augusto de Arruda Botelho Neto, National Secretary of Justice, representing the Ministry of Justice and Public Security; and  Flavio Jose Roman, representing the Attorney General's Office; and  all the others present here.  It is a great pleasure to participate in this seminar that celebrates the 25th anniversary of Law No. 9,613.  This important milestone of Brazilian legislation:  established the foundations of the Brazilian system for the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing (AML/FTP); and  created the Council for the Control of Financial Activities (Coaf), which plays a central role in this system.  Since the enactment of Law No. 9,613, Brazil has sought to keep its legal, regulatory and institutional framework in line with international standards, following the recommendations of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), represented here by its President.  The FATF was created in 1989 with the objective of establishing standards and promoting the implementation of measures to combat money laundering, terrorist financing and other threats to the integrity of the financial system. o Brazil became a full member of the FATF in 2000.  Among the recommendations issued by the Group, the methodology of the risk-based approach stands out, according to which competent authorities and the private sector should, in relation to these illicit activities:  identify, assess and understand the risks to which they are exposed; and  adopt, according to the identified risks, proportionate and appropriate measures to mitigate them.  The Central Bank of Brazil (BC) has advanced in this direction by internally consolidating the risk-based approach methodology with the issuance of BCB Circular No. 3,978, of 2020.  With continuous improvements like this, the Central Bank has concretely demonstrated its efforts to remain aligned with the best international practices aimed at combating and preventing these crimes.  But the effective fight against these illicit activities depends on joint work, carried out on several fronts, by the various participants in this system of combat and prevention.  Among them are public and private institutions, national and foreign, which over the years have contributed to important advances and structural improvements of the system.  A part of these institutions fulfills the important role of forwarding information about suspicious transactions to Coaf;  Another part works to improve regulation and controls;  While other institutions act in the conduct of investigative procedures.  I can say that this cooperation has generated very good results.  The Central Bank's performance has contributed to enabling important operations conducted by the Federal Police, the Public Prosecutor's Office and other control bodies. Coaf. In 2022 alone, more than 5.5 million communications were made, which represented 80% of all communications received by Coaf in the year.  Within the international community, the FATF monitors the progress of its members in implementing international standards through periodic mutual evaluations.  This evaluation process requires not only regulatory compliance with the recommendations, but also proof of the effectiveness of actions to combat and prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.  Brazil has just passed the 4th round of Assessments, and the results will reflect the Central Bank's strong commitment to combating and preventing these crimes.  Still in the effort to be more aligned with the international standards established by the FATF, the Central Bank has also contributed to greater adherence to the principles and norms present in international acts ratified by Brazil, such as the conventions:  the OECD (on Combating Bribery of Foreign Public Officials in International Business Transactions); and  of the UN (against Corruption).  However, despite all the advances, we are aware that we still have a lot of work ahead of us.  In the coming years, we hope to continue this continuous process of improvement.  We have advanced in a broad agenda of new technologies that have the potential to increase the traceability of operations and make the fight against and prevention of these illicit activities even more effective. o But there are challenges, as new technologies can also be used for illicit operations.  To conclude, I would like to mention that all the efforts made since the enactment of Law No. 9,613:  indicate the concreteness of Brazil's actions in relation to this issue; and  reinforce our commitment to continue this work, which will be reflected in a good performance in the FATF Mutual Evaluation rounds.  It is in this spirit that I would like to take this opportunity to once again renew, on behalf of the entire Central Bank of Brazil, our willingness to continue contributing to the evolution of the Brazilian system for the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing.  Thank you very much!

Title: Remarks by President Roberto Campos Neto in a solemn session in the Chamber of Deputies. - 207.1 Kb
text: CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL Notes by President Roberto Campos Neto for the Solemn Session in honor of the 1069th anniversary of the birth of economist and former federal deputy Roberto de Oliveira Campos (1917-2001) in the Chamber of Deputies Brasilia, August 02, 2023 Introduction  Good morning everyone!  I would like to start by greeting all the participants in this ceremony.  It is an honor to participate in this tribute to my grandfather Roberto de Oliveira Campos, who if he were alive would have turned 106 years old this year.  I thank the Chamber of Deputies for honoring him once again.  In my speech, I would like, mainly, to address my grandfather's performance as a parliamentarian and public man. Public life  Throughout his public life, my grandfather was one of the main spokesmen for liberal thought in Brazil.  His life trajectory in the public sphere is well known. o After graduating in theology and philosophy, he began his public life at Itamaraty. o During the second government of Getulio Vargas, he contributed to the creation of the National Bank for Economic Development. o He also worked in the JK government, in the preparation of the Plan of Goals. o In the Castello Branco government, he was Minister of Planning. With the Economic and Governmental Action Program (PAEG), it contributed to the stabilization of inflation and to the implementation of important structural reforms, such as tax reform and the financial system, which included a banking reform and the creation of the Central Bank of Brazil (BCB). Still as Minister of Planning, he was one of the creators of the IPEA. Throughout his public life, he was also ambassador to Washington and London. Performance in Congress In the 1980s, my grandfather began his work as a congressman. the first as a senator for his home state, Mato Grosso, between 1983 and 1991; o Then as a federal deputy for the state of Rio de Janeiro, for two terms, from 1991 to 1999.  At the beginning of his parliamentary career, he strongly criticized the market reserve created by the National Information Technology Policy, of 198423.  As a constituent senator, Roberto Campos o Acted mainly in defense:  individual and economic freedoms;  the reduction of State intervention in the economy;  technological exchange between Brazil and other countries; and  the isonomic treatment of capital, regardless of its origin; and  increased competition and efficiency in production. o He was the author of 186 amendments to the constitutional text, in the preliminary drafts and the Draft Constitution phases.  Of this total: 24 amendments were approved; and  28 amendments were partially approved. o The amendments dealt with several topics and, always in line with liberal thinking, aimed to increase efficiency in economic activity and incentives for private initiative. More specifically, the proposals sought, among other objectives:  reduce the voluntarism of the State;  make labor market relations more flexible;  increase efficiency in oil exploration in the national territory; and  to ensure homogeneous treatment of capital; o In the context of the discussions in the committees of the Constituent Assembly, the minutes of the meetings recorded several interventions against the inclusion, in the constitutional text, of preferential treatment of the State to companies with majority participation of national capital. o For him, the constitutional text should not contain provisions that limit the participation of foreign capital in the economy, since the country could not do without foreign savings and technological exchange for its development. o In the minutes of the committee meetings, their interventions contrary to the market reserve are also recorded, such as the one resulting from the National Information Technology Policy, in force at the time, and to the monopolies.  During the Constituent Assembly and in the following years, as a federal deputy and public figure, Roberto Campos harshly criticized the constitutional text. For him, the 1988 Constitution: established a wide range of rights that are not always compatible with the sources of revenue. attributed to the State a fundamental role in strategic enterprises. In its final form, it presented an anachronistic character, often not aligned with the advance of globalization and the free market, which hindered the creation of an environment favorable to free enterprise, capital accumulation and technological progress.  In addition, he disagreed with the tax and social security model contained in the constitutional text and prophesied the economic and administrative difficulties that would follow. Post-1990 period  Despite the difficulties faced by the country, Roberto Campos also saw, in his last years of life, some of his liberal visions become reality in Brazil. Although still far from a liberal model, the country was increasingly in line with his ideas. o Throughout the 90s, he witnessed the deregulation of the electricity, oil, telephone and computer sectors, and several privatizations. o He also witnessed the beginning of a large phase of foreign capital inflow into Brazil, something he has always defended. And he, who argued that the stability of inflation required a solution to the fiscal issue, also saw the Fiscal Responsibility Law approved in 2000.  Since his death in 2001, the National Congress has promoted several legislative changes towards economic freedom. o Considering the most recent period, Roberto Campos would be happy to Know the approval: the pension reform; the BC Autonomy Law; and more recently, the modernization of foreign exchange legislation.  As a technology enthusiast, my grandfather would also be pleased with the results of Pix, Open Finance, and the ongoing work for the launch of the Digital Real, within the framework of the Central Bank's innovation agenda. Conclusion  To conclude, I would like to say that Roberto Campos, throughout his public life, always remained consistent in the defense of ideas ahead of his time, which would become reality in the following years.  In the various positions he held, he always sought to prepare Brazil for the future, defending ideas and initiatives that would contribute to the construction of a more competitive, efficient and modern country.  Thank you very much.

text: CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL Rio de Janeiro (RJ), November 28, 2023 Regional Leaders Award - Rio de Janeiro ECONOMY PERSONALITY Ladies, gentlemen, good afternoon.  It is with great satisfaction that I receive the 2023 Regional Leaders Award from the LIDE Rio de Janeiro Business Council, in the Economy Personality category.  I am very happy to receive this time. o This award is, above all, a recognition of the excellent work that has been carried out by the employees of the Central Bank of Brazil.  Committed to its institutional missions, the Central Bank has worked to: o Ensure the stability of the purchasing power of our currency, o and to increase the efficiency and competitiveness of the National Financial System (SFN), thus promoting the economic well-being of society.  Faced with an environment of high inflation and uncertainties in the global scenario, the Central Bank acted in a timely manner, which has made it possible to reduce inflation at a relatively low cost, compared to other countries.  At the same time, in recent years, the Central Bank has been implementing several initiatives in its innovation agenda (our BC# Agenda) that have generated greater financial inclusion and provided the population with access to a more modern, competitive, and inclusive financial system.  Despite all the achievements, we are aware that we still have work ahead. o It is important to consolidate the process of reducing inflation, and o Advance in our agenda to modernize the financial system, whose actions include Pix, Open Finance, the modernization of foreign exchange legislation, and Drex, our digital currency.  I would like to conclude by congratulating the other winners and close by dedicating this award to the employees of the Central Bank of Brazil.  Thank you very much.
